The buyer (a creator, a DAO, a brand, a conference, a company all-hands) funds the pool as an engagement budget they already have and already spends without expecting ROI, which removes the CPM arbitrage you cannot win and removes the prize pool as CAC. You are then selling a live-event tool with a settlement rail rather than selling attention at 20-50x market rate, and the on-chain escrow becomes a real feature — the buyer's audience can verify the sponsor actually funded the prize, which is a genuine trust problem in creator giveaways. Concretely for the MVP: keep the ER, the Crank-closed windows, and the Switchboard shuffle exactly as specified; drop the nightly public show, drop Telegram, drop the Revive-for-invite mechanic entirely (replace with a free daily Revive plus an optional invite bonus that grants nothing gameplay-relevant), and pay in a spendable balance with a $25 cash-out threshold that you are honest about rather than pretending USDC-to-wallet is USDC-to-bank.

name: Bidder's Keep
pitch: A four-player dungeon crawl where you set the price of your own sword — and anyone watching the fight can buy it out of your hands, mid-swing.
coreLoop: Every item you carry has a price tag YOU set (a slider, min $1, no max). While you hold it, you pay a Harberger carry tax of 0.5% of your self-assessed price per 60 seconds of raid time, streamed out of your in-raid purse by a MagicBlock Crank. A $40 sword bleeds you ~$0.20/min. Anyone in the world — squadmates, spectators on the web feed, a bot — can hit BUY at your posted price. The item unbinds over a 2.5s glow animation, teleports to them, and USDC hits your balance instantly. The 30-second loop: watch your tax meter tick, watch the boss's health bar, watch the little BUY-pressure counter on your weapon (how many wallets have it open in a buy modal right now), and decide — reprice up and eat the bleed, or ride it and risk being disarmed at 8% boss HP. Raids are 6 minutes, 4 players. No RNG anywhere in the value path: there are no loot drops. Items enter the world only by crafting from deterministic raid materials (kill 40 skeletons, get 40 bone). Cooldowns keep it readable — an item can only be bought once per 90s, and a new owner must reprice within 30s or it auto-lists at 1.25x.
whyOnChain: Partly, honestly. The Harberger mechanic is money-native, not necessarily chain-native: the tension only exists because the price is real money you actually lose. You could build this on Stripe. What Solana specifically buys you: (1) the buy-side is the entire internet, not your MAU — a wallet that has never installed the game can snipe a sword off a streamer's back, which is where all the drama and most of the volume comes from, and that's a wallet-native audience you get for free; (2) the seizure has to be non-consensual and instant, which means an escrow program holding permanent transfer authority (Metaplex Core Transfer Delegate) rather than a database row you're asked to trust; (3) no chargebacks on a mechanic whose entire premise is involuntary sale. Call it a 70% reason. I would not claim more.
solanaPrimitives: MagicBlock Ephemeral Rollups — per-raid PDA + the 4 players' equipped Core assets delegated for the 6-minute raid; ~10ms slots so a buyout resolves visually instantly, 64KB txs so a full raid-state commit fits in one tx at settlement
MagicBlock Cranks — the per-60s Harberger tax accrual tick, on-chain, no game server heartbeat
MagicBlock Session Keys (@magicblock-labs/gum-react-sdk) — sign once at raid start, no popups for 6 minutes
Magic Router — routes spectator buyouts to the ER while the item is delegated, to L1 when it isn't
Metaplex Core (mpl-core 1.10.0) with the Transfer Delegate + Attributes plugins — ~0.0029 SOL/asset; the delegate is what makes involuntary buyout possible, Attributes carries price/durability
Kora fee relayer (Solana Foundation, shipped Apr 2026) — players hold USDC and zero SOL, fees paid in USDC
Helius DAS API — spectator inventory/feed reads
Jito bundles — atomic multi-tx settlement of raid results back to L1
LiteSVM 0.15.2 + Mollusk 0.15.0 in CI — CU benchmarking on the tax-tick instruction, since that instruction runs against every delegated item every minute
moneyFlow: IN: USDC top-up (card via a Privy/Stripe embedded wallet), spent on buying items off other players. OUT: players withdraw USDC — and only back to their own funding wallet, no arbitrary third-party sends (this is deliberate; see risk). SINKS, named: (a) the Harberger carry tax is the primary sink and it is funded by consumption, not by new entrants — a player carrying $100 of gear across 3 raids/day burns ~$0.90/day, of which 80% goes into the weekly raid prize pot and 20% to the house; (b) 3% house fee on every buyout; (c) crafting consumes materials and USDC; (d) durability repair. Team revenue: 3% of buyout volume + 20% of tax. The sustainability identity holds by construction — payouts (E) come only from the tax pot and the buyout rake, both functions of current player spend (S), never of new-user inflow. NO native token. Ever. Prices are in USDC. Per the 2025-26 record (95% average gaming-token drawdown, BattleFrens paying prizes in SOL and doing fine), the token is the liability.
firstSession: 0:00 — email login, Privy embedded wallet created silently, Kora sponsors everything; the word 'wallet' never appears. 0:20 — you're handed a Rusted Shortsword, auto-assessed at $0.00. A tooltip: 'Anyone can buy this from you for $0.00. That's fine — it's rusty.' 0:40 — tutorial raid; 30 seconds in, a scripted NPC buyer takes the sword out of your hands. You feel it. You now understand the entire game. 1:10 — you're given $3 of free credit and shown the LIVE FEED: four real raids in progress, every carried item with a price tag and a BUY button. You buy a $2.40 Bone Axe off a stranger who priced it too low. It appears in your bag, on-chain, permanently. 1:40 — the reprice screen: 'What's it worth to you?' You set $6. The game shows: 'Carry cost: $0.03/min. Buy pressure: 2 wallets watching.' 2:10 — you queue for a real 6-minute raid with your $6 axe. 2:40 — someone offers to buy it at 3:20 into the fight and you have to decide, live, whether to reprice to $15 mid-combat. That decision, made under a boss timer, is the product.
viralMechanic: Spectating is a paid role, not a courtesy. 'Fences' don't play raids — they watch the live feed and snipe underpriced gear, and the entry cost is $2 and zero skill. That means every player has a structural reason to drag in the friend who doesn't play action games: you tell them 'watch my raid and buy my axe back if someone tries to take it,' which is a real, useful job and it makes them a customer. Second loop: every buyout emits a named event with a 6-second replay clip ('@dana bought your Bonecleaver for $34 while you were at 12% HP') that is one tap to share and structurally humiliating, which is the same reason Fomo3D and pump.fun screenshots travelled. Third: because the buy-side is permissionless, third-party sniper bots and price-tracking sites will exist without you building them, and they are free distribution.
mvpScope: 2-4 weeks, web only. IN: one 6-minute dungeon, one boss, three weapon archetypes, 4-player squads; Harberger pricing + tax crank + buyout, fully on MagicBlock ER against a per-raid PDA with Core assets delegated; a spectator web view with a live BUY button; Privy embedded wallet + Kora gasless + devnet USDC, flipped to mainnet USDC for a closed 200-player test. Anchor 1.1.2 (@anchor-lang/core, NOT @coral-xyz), Surfpool + LiteSVM for tests, @solana/kit 7.1.1 client, Codama-generated TS. CUT: crafting trees, cosmetics, progression, mobile, leaderboards, seasons, marketplaces, anything with a token. The entire test is one question, answerable in two weeks: when a stranger takes your weapon mid-boss, do you rage-quit or do you immediately queue again to earn it back? If it's rage-quit, kill the project on day 21.
biggestRisk: That the core mechanic is infuriating rather than thrilling — theft-with-compensation is the most emotionally dangerous mechanic in game design, and Harberger taxes have never been shipped in anything people play for fun. Secondary and nearly as lethal: this is a money-transmission risk, not a gambling risk. Custodying player USDC and permitting withdrawal is what pulls in state MTLs (~$50k-150k/state across 40+ states) and FinCEN MSB analysis — the research is explicit that this kills more small teams than securities law. Mitigation is architectural: non-custodial, withdrawals only to the originating wallet, no P2P transfers except item trades, no fiat off-ramp built by us. Third: MagicBlock's ER trust model (fraud proofs, DA, undelegation-under-validator-failure) is undocumented — this design routes real USDC through it, so that is a blocking pre-ship question to MagicBlock, not a launch-week detail.

critique.name: Bidder's Keep
technicalBlockers: ATOMIC BUYOUT IS ARCHITECTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE AS PITCHED. MagicBlock's own FAQ: 'Every account on Solana is readable on ER, while only delegated accounts can be changed on ER within an atomic transaction.' A spectator buyout must debit the buyer's USDC AND transfer the Core asset in one tx, which means the buyer's token account must be delegated to THAT raid's ER. An account carries one delegation record, so a spectator cannot have the same $50 live across 4 concurrent raids. The pitch's central claim — 'the buy-side is the entire internet; a wallet that has never installed the game can snipe a sword off a streamer's back' — then requires either (a) per-raid pre-funded escrow, which fragments a fence's bankroll N ways and forces an undelegate/redelegate round trip (0.0003 SOL/session + 0.0001 SOL/commit + L1 settlement at 350ms+) every time they switch raids, or (b) Magic Actions settling payment on L1 while the item moves in the ER — which is NON-ATOMIC and opens a straight theft window in both directions. Neither delivers the demo. This does not appear in a 1-raid MVP; it appears in week 5.

ACTION COMBAT OVER A SEQUENCER. 10ms slots buy nothing you can feel. A player at 40-150ms RTT to the nearest MagicBlock region gets 5-9 frames of input delay at 60fps in a chain-authoritative model with no rollback netcode (you cannot roll back committed sequencer state). Action games treat >4 frames as uncompetitive. The 'mid-swing' fantasy is a netcode problem the ER does not solve.

THE 'BUY-PRESSURE COUNTER' IS OFF-CHAIN AND FREE TO SPOOF. 'How many wallets have it open in a buy modal right now' is a client-side event on your server. A bot fleet opening 50 fake modals costs ~$0 and panics a player into repricing $6 → $20, tripling their carry bleed. You have shipped a zero-cost griefing lever that directly farms your own primary sink.

ER state streaming is not L1 Geyser/Yellowstone — the spectator feed and any third-party sniper bot need a MagicBlock-side read path, and whoever colocates with the ER validator sees posted prices first. There is no way to price that advantage away: ER base fee is 0 SOL/tx, so there is no priority auction and no economic tie-break on a contested buyout.

MagicBlock ER trust model (fraud proofs, DA, undelegation under validator failure) is undocumented. The team flags this correctly, but this design routes live USDC custody through it, which makes it a blocking answer, not an open question.
economicHoles: THE PRIMARY SINK IS MIS-STATED BY EXACTLY 10x. 0.5% per 60s × a 6-minute raid = 3.0% of self-assessed value per raid. $100 of gear × 3 raids/day = $9.00/day, not the '$0.90/day' written in moneyFlow. That is $270/month of pure bleed on a $100 loadout — roughly 5-10x the ARPPU of a top-grossing mobile title, charged to the MEDIAN player as a loss. Every retention and revenue number built on that paragraph is off by an order of magnitude.

THE TAX BASE IS BACKWARDS. Tax accrues per '60 seconds of RAID time.' A spectator or fence who never raids holds inventory at ZERO carry cost forever. The optimal strategy in Bidder's Keep is therefore: never play the game. The 'Fences' the viral mechanic proudly recruits are a structurally advantaged extractive class farming the only people who pay the sink — the Axie manager/scholar split rediscovered, with the extractors on the outside of the game.

80% OF THE 'SINK' IS NOT A SINK. Tax splits 80% to the weekly prize pot, 20% house. Net destruction is only 20% of tax plus the 3% buyout rake. So this is a redistribution tournament with a ~20% rake: the median player loses 100% of their carry tax to the top of the ladder. 'Payouts come only from current spend, never new-user inflow' is true and irrelevant — a negative-sum PvP transfer churns players just as fast as an inflationary faucet, it just kills them from the bottom up instead of the top down.

DETERMINISTIC CRAFTING CAPS ITEM VALUE AT LABOR COST, WHICH COLLAPSES THE MARKET EITHER WAY. Items enter only by crafting from deterministic materials ('kill 40 skeletons, get 40 bone'). If crafting is ungated, the arbitrage-free resale price of any item equals its crafting cost — buyouts clear at cost, nobody is ever profitably sniped, tax on near-zero self-assessments is near-zero, and there is no prize pot. If crafting IS gated, items are scarce, and a 3%-per-raid tax on a scarce item makes playing strictly dominated by hoarding. Both branches break.

SNIPER BOTS SOLVE THIS IN AN AFTERNOON AND DELETE THE PRODUCT. A bot subscribed to ER state buys anything priced below resale, instantly and always. Equilibrium: every human must price at or above true market value at all times, so nobody is ever bought except by fat-finger, and everyone pays maximum carry tax on maximum self-assessment. The fun (getting robbed) disappears; the cost (the bleed) is maximized. Rational play converges to the least entertaining possible state.

There is no genuine buy-side demand. A spectator who buys a sword mid-raid cannot use it — they are a flipper needing a greater fool, in a market with a hard crafting-cost price ceiling and zero carry cost for non-players. That is a hot-potato market with no fundamental underneath it.
legalFlags: MONEY TRANSMISSION, and worse than the team's own read. Buyouts move USDC from person A to person B through an operator-controlled escrow program holding permanent Transfer Delegate authority. FinCEN's administrator/transmitter analysis turns on accepting and transmitting value between two persons, and 'non-custodial' is a hard argument to make when your program can seize an asset without the owner's signature. 40+ state MTLs at $50k-150k each is the right order of magnitude; withdrawal-only-to-funding-wallet is a real mitigation and not a cure.

PAID-ENTRY PRIZE CONTEST — unflagged in the brief. The 'weekly raid prize pot' is funded by real USDC bled from players and paid out on raid performance: consideration, prize, outcome. Even under a skill-predominance reading that lands on the ~10-state skill-gaming exclusion list plus Florida (Ch. 849 bars wagering on games of skill). Needs geofencing and counsel that the brief does not budget for.

'NO CHARGEBACKS' IS FALSE. The card on-ramp (Privy/Stripe) has a fiat leg with full chargeback rights regardless of on-chain finality; crypto on-ramps run 3-8% dispute/fraud rates and the PSP pushes that loss to the merchant. A mechanic whose premise is involuntary sale will also generate genuine UDAP/consumer-protection complaints ('a stranger took my $40 sword') that card networks read as merchant fault.

Metaplex Core Transfer Delegate with permanent seizure authority is functionally the same primitive family as the Token-2022 Permanent Delegate powering 2026's largest automated rug family. Expect wallet and marketplace scam-flagging on any asset your program can move without the holder's consent, plus the user suspicion that comes with it.
critique.priorArt: Harberger taxation has been shipped repeatedly and has never once retained a player. simondlr's This Artwork Is Always On Sale (2019, the canonical implementation) produced roughly 18.4 ETH of lifetime patronage across years — a rounding error, and it is art, not a game. Wildcards.world built the Harberger *game* (always-for-sale NFT animals funding conservation via the tax); its blog goes silent mid-2022 and the project is effectively dormant. Eric Wall's Orb (April 2023) carried a 300%/yr Harberger tax and the holder RELINQUISHED it under the burden (covered by The Block) — Bidder's Keep charges 0.5%/min, which annualizes on play-time to roughly 3,000-11,000%/yr, i.e. 10-35x the rate that broke the Orb. EIP-5320 (Harberger NFTs, 2022) was proposed and never adopted. RadicalxChange's own NYC Monopoly playtest concluded Harberger is 'a hard sell to players' with serious UX concerns. On the full-loot half: OSRS's Wilderness is the one durable example and works precisely because it is opt-in and spatially bounded; Bidder's Keep has no safe zone, and the record on unbounded full-loot (Legends of Aria, Sea of Thieves forums, Ashes threads) is a consistent new-player-churn story.
critique.suggestedFix: Tax wall-clock possession, not raid time, and cut the rate roughly 10x (≈0.05%/min of wall-clock ≈ 0.7%/day). That single change fixes three things simultaneously: it destroys the hoarder arbitrage that currently makes non-players strictly advantaged over players, it brings the bleed from $270/month to ~$20/month on a $100 loadout, and it moves the sink onto inventory rather than onto the act of playing. Then stop trying to settle payment inside a per-raid ER: run ONE persistent ER for the whole live-feed session with a single shared escrow vault delegated to it, so every fence's balance is atomically writable against every raid, and treat each raid PDA as just another account in that ER. If MagicBlock cannot support that shape, fall back to sealed-bid buyouts that CLEAR at raid settlement on L1 — you lose 'mid-swing' instantaneity, you keep the entire Harberger tension, and the atomicity blocker disappears.

name: Longshot
pitch: A 60-second gladiator duel where the crowd's money is the handicap: the more people back you, the weaker you start.
coreLoop: 16 human fighters, single-elimination bracket, one tournament every 30 minutes, ~20 minutes end to end. Each duel has a 90-second pre-fight market: a constant-product AMM on two outcome shares, seeded with 200 units of house liquidity, open to anyone including bots. At the bell the market price is FROZEN and converted directly into the fight rules: effective HP = 100 x (1 + 1.2 x (0.5 - implied_prob)). A fighter the crowd prices at 20% walks in with 136 HP; the 80% favourite walks in with 64. Then a separate free-floating in-fight market opens and does NOT touch stats — that's where the pure trading happens, tick by tick, while a three-button melee plays out at 10ms in the rollup. The 30-second loop for a trader: read the bracket, decide whether you're predicting or sabotaging (buying the favourite is a paid attack that nerfs them — you are literally spending money to break someone's legs, and you lose your stake if it works too well), place, then watch the HP bars set. The 30-second loop for a fighter: you see the crowd money moving in your pre-fight lobby and know exactly how much respect is about to cost you.
whyOnChain: The odds ARE the rules. That is the whole design, and it is why an operator-run version cannot exist: if the house computes the odds and the house computes the HP, every fighter who loses will — correctly — suspect the handicap was tuned, and no fighter will accept a system where an invisible number decides how much health they get. It has to be a public AMM anyone can audit and anyone can trade against. Second: the trade and the combat have to be one atomic state machine. HP recomputation from an AMM price, at the bell, deterministically, is a single instruction in one rollup — a Web2 server calling a chain would introduce exactly the gap where fixing happens. Third: a permissionless market staffs itself with algorithmic traders at 4am, which is the only way a market this thin gets prices at all. Where it is weak: in the play-money v1 (see moneyFlow) the money is not real, so points 1 and 3 hold but point 2 is a convenience. I'd rate this the most chain-native of the three ideas on mechanism, and the most legally constrained on money.
solanaPrimitives: MagicBlock Ephemeral Rollups — the duel and the AMM live in the same delegated account set; ~10ms slots for combat, and the bell instruction reads the AMM price and writes HP atomically inside one runtime. 64KB ER txs mean a full fight-log commit lands in one settlement tx
MagicBlock Cranks — bracket advancement, the 90s market window open/close, and the frozen-price snapshot at the bell, all on-chain timers with no game server
MagicBlock Session Keys — a spectator signs once per tournament and trades 15 duels without a popup
Metaplex Core (mpl-core 1.10.0) — the fighter character, with the Attributes plugin holding lifetime record; Attributes are read by the matchmaker so seeding is verifiable
Bubblegum V2 (mpl-bubblegum 5.1.0) SOULBOUND compressed NFTs — tournament trophies and streak badges, non-tradeable by construction, ~$500 per million assets vs $15-30k for the same in Core
Kora fee relayer — traders hold only USDC (or, in v1, nothing at all) and never see a SOL balance
Solana Attestation Service — one free daily chip allotment per verified human; without this the free-currency version is farmed to death in a week
Helius LaserStream / Yellowstone gRPC — the public odds ticker and the open bot API (verify wire compatibility yourself; the two are reported as not actually interchangeable)
Pinocchio 0.11.2 for the per-tick combat instruction — it runs 100x/second per duel, so CUs are literally the operating cost
moneyFlow: Be blunt: v1 has no money flow, on purpose. Fighters and traders use 'Chips' — 1,000 free per verified human per day, no purchase path of any kind, no cash-out, weekly leaderboard reset, cosmetic-only prizes. That is not a sweepstakes (there is nothing to buy, so there is no dual-currency system), it is a free game, and Manifold Markets is the existence proof that play-money prediction markets retain. Studio revenue in v1: $0. It is a two-month test of one hypothesis — is a self-negating market fun. IF it is, v2 is one of two paths, both expensive: (a) fighter-side only — $5 seat fees into a skill-tournament prize pool with a rake, geofenced, with spectator markets staying play-money forever, or (b) a real-money market under a Curacao CGA licence (~$50k-200k, 6-12 months, and it confers no right to serve US/UK/most EU players) with hard geofencing. Sinks in v1: chips are burned on every AMM trade fee (0.3%) and expire daily, so the float cannot inflate. No native token under any version.
firstSession: 0:00 — you land on a live tournament, no login. A duel is running; you see two HP bars at 136 and 64 with a caption 'the crowd made him weak.' 0:30 — a market window opens on the next fight. To place, you tap once; email login creates a Privy embedded wallet and Solana Attestation Service issues your daily 1,000 chips in the background. You never see a seed phrase or a SOL balance (Kora). 0:50 — you buy 200 chips on the underdog. The odds move visibly because your 200 chips is 12% of the book. You see the projected HP bars shift in real time as a direct consequence of your click. That is the hook and it lands inside one minute. 1:30 — the bell rings, HP freezes at your numbers, and the fight you shaped plays out in 60 seconds. 2:30 — you're offered a fighter seat in the next bracket, free, and the game shows you your own projected HP based on the market's current read of a total unknown (it's ~50/50, so 100 HP). 3:00 — you're in a duel with strangers' money sitting on you.
viralMechanic: Sabotage is a gift you give a friend, and it costs money. 'I bought 500 chips on you so you'd start at 61 HP, good luck' is a message players will actually send, and it requires the friend to be in the game to receive it. That is a structural referral: the pre-fight market gives every trader a reason to recruit a specific named fighter to bully. Second loop: because pre-fight prices are manipulation-by-design, a rival trader's over-buy is publicly visible and creates a named grudge with a scoreboard attached. Third: the odds feed is a public on-chain AMM, so bot-builders, odds-scrapers and clip accounts spin up without a BD deal — the same free composability distribution the research credits as one of the few real crypto advantages.
mvpScope: 2-4 weeks. IN: 8-fighter bracket (not 16), 60-second duels, three-button combat, one arena; the constant-product AMM and combat in a single MagicBlock ER program; bell-freeze HP coupling with a tunable k exposed in an admin config because k is the whole balance problem; free chips + Attestation gate; spectator web view with a live odds ticker; @solana/kit 7.1.1, Anchor 1.1.2, Codama clients, LiteSVM tests. CUT: real money entirely, the in-fight free-floating market (ship it in week 5 — the frozen coupling is the novel part), fighter NFTs, trophies, progression, mobile, LP incentives. Success test: do spectators come back for tournament #6 without any payout, and do fighters accept the handicap instead of quitting?
biggestRisk: The fixed point may be degenerate. A market whose consensus is self-punishing might simply refuse to have a price — if k is high, informed traders won't take a position because their own fill damages it, and the book goes empty; if k is low, the coupling is a gimmick nobody feels. There is a workable band in between and I don't know how wide it is, which is why k is a config value on day one. Second risk: fighters resent the mechanic. Losing because Twitter liked you is a story you tell once and a reason to quit twice. Third: the moment real money touches the spectator side, this is wagering on the outcome of a contest — plainly gambling in nearly every US state, and the Kalshi Third Circuit preemption does NOT reach it (that shelter attaches to CFTC DCM registration, which costs eight figures). The dual-currency 'sweepstakes' workaround is being criminalised in real time — NY Class E felony, Oklahoma felony, Louisiana $100k plus five years, and Louisiana and Oklahoma name suppliers, geolocation vendors and promoters as liable parties. So: free chips, or a licence and a geofence. There is no third door, and any plan that assumes there is one is the risk.

critique.name: Longshot
technicalBlockers: THE HEADLINE SCREENSHOT IS OFF-EQUILIBRIUM BY CONSTRUCTION. Solve the fixed point p* = w(skill, HP(p)) under a standard log-odds duel model (λ=1, HP ratio mapping ~1:1 into log-odds): an evenly matched pair (55/45 unhandicapped) settles at p*=0.531 → 96 HP vs 104. A solid favourite (60/40) → p*=0.563 → 92 vs 108. A DOMINANT 3:1 favourite (75/25) → p*=0.667 → 80 vs 120. You need a fighter who wins 90% unhandicapped before the market prices them at 0.806 and you get the advertised 63-vs-137. In an efficient book the mechanic is invisible — a 4-8% HP nudge nobody can feel. It is only dramatic when the book is WRONG. The design therefore has exactly two states, 'imperceptible' and 'random punishment,' and the marketing image lives only in the second.

SABOTAGE IS RELIABLY NEGATIVE-EV, SO NOBODY RATIONALLY SUPPLIES IT. Pushing a 200/200 CPMM (k=40,000) from 0.5 to 0.8 costs exactly 200 units of collateral and yields ~300 shares at an average price of 0.667. But you have just cut that fighter to 64 HP, so their true win probability is now roughly 0.30-0.35 → expected value ~100 against 200 spent, about a 50% expected loss per sabotage. It is a pure spite purchase. So all order flow is spite or free chips, the house's 200-unit LP faces informed flow with no noise traders to farm, and a real-money v2 has no rational bid side at all.

MANIPULATION IS ABSURDLY CHEAP AT THE STATED SEEDING. Same CPMM: 45 units moves the handicap to 88 HP, 106 units to 76 HP, 200 units to 64 HP, 400 units to 52 HP. Against 1,000 FREE chips per verified human per day, ONE account can dictate the handicap of five duels a day or crush any single duel twice over. There is no capital constraint on the sabotage side because the capital is free.

FIGHTER DUTY CYCLE IS 3-7%. 16 fighters, single elimination, one tournament per 30 minutes: eight of your sixteen humans are finished after a 60-second fight and then wait ~28 minutes. Median fighter engagement is 60-120 seconds per half hour. You must staff 32 skilled melee players per hour just to run the format, and half of them are punished for showing up. Supersize.gg, the ER's own proof point, is continuous for exactly this reason.

3-BUTTON MELEE OVER A SEQUENCER. 10ms slots do not fix 40-150ms RTT, and there is no rollback against committed state. You are shipping a fighting game with 5-9 frames of input lag, and the entire handicap mechanic depends on players believing the fight was decided by their play rather than by the network.

The firstSession script contradicts the anti-sybil design: '0:30 — email login… Solana Attestation Service issues your daily 1,000 chips in the background.' SAS/Civic attestation is a document-plus-liveness flow, not a background process. Expect 30-60% funnel drop and a per-verification cost, on a product whose stated v1 revenue is $0.
economicHoles: CONTESTANTS CAN TRADE THE CONTEST THEY CONTROL, AND IT IS THE DOMINANT STRATEGY. A fighter spends 200 chips buying shares in their OPPONENT: opponent drops to 64 HP, fighter gets 136 HP, fighter very likely wins and advances. The shares go to zero, but if the tournament prize is worth more than 200 chips, self-funded opponent-nerfing dominates for every fighter in every duel. Both fighters do it, the prices cancel, both end near 100 HP, and both have burned 200 chips. The pitch frames this as a feature; it is a prisoner's-dilemma tax on your fighter base, and the instant money is real it is textbook match-fixing.

v1 revenue is $0 by design and both v2 paths are five- to six-figure regulatory projects. That is a two-month research grant, not a business model — and it means the SUCCESS outcome of the MVP is a $50k-200k bill and 6-12 months of licensing before a dollar arrives.

Free chips plus an SAS gate raises sybil cost without eliminating it, and the ecosystem's own caveat on SAS is that schema standards are inconsistent and low-quality attestations are manipulable. With a 1,000-chip daily float per human against a 200-unit book, a 20-identity farm owns the handicap of every duel on the platform.

Liquidity fragments badly: round 1 runs 8 parallel duels, no trader can watch 8 markets, and 200 units of house liquidity per book means each individual market is thinner than one motivated griefer's daily chip allowance.
legalFlags: Real-money spectator markets on the outcome of a human contest are sports/event wagering in effectively every US state. The brief's read is correct, and the Kalshi Third Circuit preemption genuinely does not reach you absent CFTC DCM registration (eight figures).

THE MATCH-FIXING VECTOR IS LICENSE-DISQUALIFYING, NOT MERELY RISKY. No gaming authority — Curacao CGA included, and certainly nothing in a regulated market — will license a wagering product in which contestants can trade the market and thereby ALTER THE RULES OF THE CONTEST. Integrity monitoring is the first question every regulator asks. Path (b) is not just expensive; as specified it is unlicensable.

The dual-currency sweepstakes workaround is being criminalized in real time (NY Class E felony, Oklahoma felony, Louisiana $100k plus five years, with suppliers, geolocation vendors and promoters named as liable). Directly on point: MANIFOLD MARKETS launched real-cash Sweepcash in September 2024 and SHUT IT DOWN on 28 March 2025 citing legal and complexity issues, reverting to pure play-money. The closest operator running this exact experiment tried the money door and retreated within seven months.

If fighters pay $5 seat fees into a prize pool (path a) while spectators trade a market on those same fighters, you have a paid contest and a wagering market on it in one product. Regulators treat that combination as an aggravating fact, not two separable ones.
critique.priorArt: No prior art found for the specific mechanic — a prediction market whose price IS the rule set. I searched game-design and betting literature; the nearest real things are conventional handicap betting (where the handicap is set to balance the market, not derived from it) and audience-affects-game formats (Choice Chamber, Rival Peak, streamer-vs-chat), none of which are markets. That novelty is real and is the best thing about this concept. The two adjacent existence proofs cut in opposite directions: MANIFOLD MARKETS proves play-money prediction markets retain at genuine scale (millions of users, billions of Mana traded monthly) — and proves the real-money version is where you die, having launched Sweepcash in September 2024 and killed it in March 2025. RuneScape's Duel Arena is the other precedent: player-versus-player staking, enormously popular, and removed by Jagex because it became a gambling and scamming vector. Nobody has shipped the self-negating market, and the equilibrium analysis above suggests the reason is that it neutralizes itself.
critique.suggestedFix: Stop making it a FORECAST market and make it an AUCTION ON THE HANDICAP. Self-negation is the whole problem: a market punished for being right converges to a fixed point where the handicap is a 4-8% nudge and the price no longer carries information about anything. Instead sell the handicap directly — spectators bid chips to add or remove HP from a named fighter, the money goes to the PRIZE POOL rather than paying out on the outcome, and the largest sabotage buyer is publicly credited on the fight card. That preserves everything genuinely good here (the crowd's money is the handicap; sabotage as a social act; 'I bought 500 chips on you so you'd start at 61 HP'), removes the degenerate fixed point entirely, removes the negative-EV problem because nobody was expecting a payout, and — critically — removes both the wagering-on-outcome characterization and the contestant-trading integrity hole, because there is no outcome contract left to trade. You lose the odds ticker and the bot-API composability. Take the trade.

name: Cave-In
pitch: Dig deeper for a bigger payday while your tunnel visibly weakens — and every other player can see exactly when it's weak enough to blow up and take your haul.
coreLoop: You run up to two mine shafts. Every 2 seconds an on-chain crank ticks: your shaft descends, ore accrues at D^1.4/100 per tick, and structural integrity decays at 0.002 x D per tick. At 20m you earn a trickle and can sit for two minutes; at 100m you earn 6 ore/tick and you have roughly 20 seconds of integrity left. When integrity drops below 1.00, your shaft turns RED on a global map every player is watching. Any other player can then spend 100 ore to detonate it: detonator takes 35% of your accumulated ore, 25% goes to the season pot, and you keep 40%. First valid detonation in the rollup wins — a genuine latency race at 10ms slots, which is MEV as a playable skill. Your three verbs, every ~30 seconds: SHORE (spend 50 x D ore for +0.25 integrity, banking nothing), SURFACE (bank your ore permanently, 5% fee), or PUSH (go deeper, earn more, shrink your window). While you're doing that you're also scanning the red shafts on the map, because hunting is more profitable than mining and the reaction window is a few seconds. There is zero randomness in this game. None. Every threat has a username.
whyOnChain: About 60% of a reason, and I'll show my work. A Web2 version is fully buildable and would play identically. What actually breaks: (1) nobody believes the decay curve isn't tuned against them, and nobody believes the operator's own bot isn't first in the liquidation queue — this is a game where the entire product is choosing to trust a public liquidation queue, and 'trust us' is not a feature you can ship; (2) you lose the third-party keeper-bot ecosystem, and the predator side has to be staffed at 4am or the miner side is boring; (3) settling a season prize pool to players in 60 countries without a payments team. What does NOT justify it: 'players own their shafts' (they don't, meaningfully), and there is no asset here worth tokenising. If you build this and the on-chain part is only the settlement, you have built a Web2 game with a wallet — and that would be an acceptable outcome, just don't lie about it in the deck.
solanaPrimitives: MagicBlock Ephemeral Rollups — the detonation race is the game, and at ~10ms slots the winner is decided by reaction plus routing rather than by whoever's tx happened to land in the same 350ms L1 slot. Delegate each active shaft PDA for the duration of the dig

One PDA per shaft, never a global map account — the 12M CU per-writable-account per-block cap is the binding constraint here, not the 100M block limit. A shared world-state account would cap the game at a few hundred concurrent diggers. The map is read-side only
MagicBlock Cranks — the 2-second decay/accrual tick, on-chain, so the decay schedule is public code rather than a server loop
MagicBlock Session Keys — one signature per dig session
Kora fee relayer — zero-SOL players; a shore-up or a detonation must never prompt for gas
ZK Compression (Light Protocol) — millions of shaft records and tick receipts at ~1000x less than standard accounts; this game generates a lot of low-value state
Jito bundles (5 txs, atomic, same slot) — season settlement, so ore-to-leaderboard-to-payout can't half-apply
Solana Attestation Service (Civic) — one verified human, one prize claim. Without this, the highest-EV strategy is running 40 shafts and your own detonator bot against yourself
Yellowstone gRPC / Helius LaserStream — the public red-shaft feed and the open keeper-bot API (budget $500-6,000/mo for streaming at scale; it is a five-figure annual line item)
Pinocchio 0.11.2 for the tick instruction, Mollusk 0.15.0 CU benchmarks in CI — the tick runs against every live shaft every 2s, so a 3k-CU regression is a direct increase in cost of goods sold

Deliberately NOT used: Pyth or any price oracle. Per the research, pegging in-game value to SOL/USD imports oracle latency and a manipulation surface; ore is a purely internal unit of account and touches USD only at the season boundary
moneyFlow: IN: a $10 USDC expedition ticket per 7-day season, straight into the season prize pool. That is the only inflow. OUT: at season end, banked ore ranks a leaderboard and the pool pays the top 20% on a 30/15/10/... schedule; house rake 12%. Ore is never withdrawable and never has a spot price — it is a score, not a currency, which is what keeps this out of 'leveraged retail product' territory and out of money transmission. SINKS, named: 25% of every cave-in haul is destroyed outright, shoring costs are pure ore destruction, and the 5% surfacing fee burns. Critically, payouts (E) are capped at 0.88 x ticket revenue (S) by construction — the ore faucet can inflate infinitely and it cannot inflate the payout, because the pool is fixed at season start. This is the exact failure Axie could not escape (5x more SLP minted than burned, ~18-19% monthly inflation, SLP -99%) and it is structurally impossible here. No native token. USDC in, USDC out, ore is scoreboard.
firstSession: 0:00 — email login, embedded wallet, Kora sponsorship; no seed phrase, no SOL. 0:15 — free practice shaft, no ticket needed. You watch two bars: ore climbing, integrity falling. 0:45 — the game deliberately lets you die: your practice shaft goes red and a scripted hunter blows it 4 seconds later, taking 60% of your haul, with their name on the explosion. 1:10 — you're shown the global map for the first time: 30 live shafts, six of them red, timers counting. You detonate one and take 35% of a stranger's ore. The theft feels excellent and takes one tap. 1:40 — the real decision screen: 'Dig shallow and safe, or deep and hunted?' with the actual numbers shown (at 100m: 6 ore/tick, ~20s of integrity). 2:20 — $10 ticket, one tap, Apple Pay through the embedded wallet. 2:40 — you're in the live season with two shafts and a map full of targets, and you have already been both prey and predator.
viralMechanic: Grudges, and they're structural. Every cave-in is signed — the detonator's name is on the explosion, on your feed, and in a permanent GRUDGES tab that tracks who has taken how much from you and offers a one-tap 'hunt them' filter on the map. Revenge is the retention loop and it requires the other person to keep playing. Second: the CREW mechanic. Two players share a shaft, split ore 70/30, and one of them watches the map while the other digs — which halves your reaction time and roughly doubles your safe depth. That is a real, quantified, selfish reason to text a friend at 11pm, not a referral banner. Third: keeper bots. Anyone can run one for $1/day, they earn a reduced 20% bounty (vs 35% for humans, so the predator side stays human-flavoured), and bot operators write blog posts and dashboards that acquire players for free.
mvpScope: 2-4 weeks. IN: one depth curve, one shaft type, the 2s crank tick, the red-shaft global map, detonation with the latency race running on a real MagicBlock devnet ER, surfacing, shoring, a 7-day closed season with a $5 ticket and 200 invited players. Anchor 1.1.2 with the hot tick instruction hand-written in Pinocchio, Surfpool + LiteSVM tests, Mollusk CU benchmarks from commit one, @solana/kit 7.1.1 + Codama client, web only. CUT: crew mode, keeper-bot API, gear NFTs, attestation (invite list substitutes), mobile, cosmetics, multiple seasons, everything about a marketplace. Success test: what fraction of a 200-player season is still opening shafts on day 6, and — the real one — does anyone voluntarily dig past the depth where the math says surface?
biggestRisk: That the predator side gets fully automated and the game stops having people in it. Bots will always beat humans on a 10ms latency race, and the second miners believe they're farming against machines, the drama evaporates and it's just a decay curve. The 20%-vs-35% bounty split is a mitigation, not a solution, and I don't have a clean answer. Second risk: regulatory look-through. The design is careful — deterministic, zero chance, entry fee into a fixed prize pool, which is the Skillz structure and skill-predominant on its face — but it FEELS like leveraged trading, and regulators judge what a product functionally is, not what you call it. PrizePicks paid ~$15M to New York and exited for exactly that reason; restructuring worked for them, labelling did not. Practical consequence: geofence the states that make this hard (the roughly ten on the standard skill-gaming exclusion list, plus Florida, which bars wagering on skill games by statute), age-gate, ship responsible-gaming tooling, and budget a real multi-jurisdiction opinion. Third: 12M CU per writable account per block will bite the first time a hundred people race to detonate the same shaft — that shaft's PDA is a hot account and the race becomes a fee auction. Design the tie-break before launch, not after.

critique.name: Cave-In
technicalBlockers: THE SHORE VERB IS DOMINATED BY ROUGHLY 500:1 AT EVERY PLAYABLE DEPTH — A LIVE SPEC BUG. Run the published numbers: shoring costs 50×D ore for +0.25 integrity, and integrity decays 0.002×D per tick, so +0.25 buys exactly 125/D ticks REGARDLESS of depth. At D=100 that is 1.25 ticks = 2.5 SECONDS of extra life for 5,000 ore, which is 792 ticks (~26 minutes) of mining output at that depth. Value bought over value spent: 0.002 at D=100, 0.004 at D=20, 0.001 at D=500. Break-even is at D≈10,119m, where decay is 20.2/tick and you die in the same tick. Your three-verb loop is a two-verb loop (PUSH/SURFACE) on day one and the defensive counterplay the tension depends on does not exist. Note also that detonating someone costs 100 ore while defending costs 5,000 — predation is 50x cheaper than defense at D=100.

ZERO RANDOMNESS PLUS FULL INFORMATION EQUALS A CLOSED-FORM OPTIMAL POLICY. The design is proud of having no RNG anywhere. The consequence is that optimal stopping depth is a solvable calculus problem with one answer, it will be posted in Discord by day 2, and every competent player will run the identical line. The stated success test — 'does anyone voluntarily dig past the depth where the math says surface?' — answers itself: no, and anyone who does is simply wrong.

HUMANS WIN APPROXIMATELY 0% OF CONTESTED DETONATIONS, SO THE 35%/20% BOUNTY SPLIT IS A NO-OP. Budget the human path: 200ms visual reaction + 16ms frame + 20-100ms client network + tx propagation ≈ 250-350ms. A colocated bot reacts in 10-30ms. At 10ms ER slots that is a 20-35 slot head start; the bot detonates within ~30ms of integrity crossing 1.00, before a human client has RENDERED the red state. The differential bounty only matters if humans ever win the race, so their expected bounty is 0 × 35% = 0. The brief lists this as its biggest risk; the arithmetic says it is a certainty.

THE ER HAS NO FEE MARKET, WHICH MAKES THE RACE WORSE. MagicBlock public nodes charge 0 SOL base fee per ER tx, so there is no priority auction and no economic tie-break — spamming detonate against every red shaft costs literally nothing, and the winner is decided by jitter and proximity to the MagicBlock validator (regions: Asia, EU, US). A US player racing an EU-hosted ER is ~80ms = 8 slots behind before anyone reacts. The brief's concern about '12M CU per writable account turning into a fee auction' is misdirected: that cap is an L1 scheduler property, and inside the ER the failure is the opposite — no auction at all.

Cross-shaft interaction forces co-delegation. Detonation writes both attacker and victim PDAs, and only delegated accounts are atomically writable in an ER, so every live shaft must sit in the SAME ER. Fine at MVP scale, but it means the 'shard state per player' guidance is structurally unavailable to you: one sequencer, one region, one failure domain, and the region choice permanently advantages one continent's bots.
economicHoles: THE SPEC CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THE SEASON POT. moneyFlow says 'payouts are capped at 0.88 × ticket revenue by construction, because the pool is fixed at season start,' while coreLoop says '25% goes to the season pot' on every cave-in. Both cannot be true. If detonated ore raises the pot, the pot is not fixed and the sustainability argument fails; if it is burned, say burned. As written, the primary sink is documented as a faucet.

'ORE IS A SCORE, NOT A CURRENCY' IS AN ASSERTION, NOT A FACT. Ore has a computable shadow price of (0.88 × ticket revenue) ÷ (total banked ore at season end), and players will compute it by hour six. That makes the 100-ore detonation fee a real-money cost and the 35% bounty a real-money transfer between two persons effected by your program — the FinCEN 'transmission between persons' fact pattern, not the closed-loop virtual-currency safe harbor the design is reaching for. Expect account OTC markets on top.

SYBIL IS PROFITABLE AT THE STATED POT SIZES. 200 players × $10 = $2,000; after the 12% rake, $1,760; top prize at 30% = $528. Two shafts per human with attestation gating PRIZE CLAIMS only. Acquiring 25 attested identities (KYC-farm rates are a well-documented category; call it $10-20 each) plus 25 tickets costs roughly $500-750 and yields 50 of 200 shafts. That fleet self-detonates its own shafts, destroying only its internal 25% so no outsider ever collects from it, while harvesting 35% off every external red shaft. Against a $528 top prize plus the rest of the top-20% schedule, that is positive EV.

THE CREW MECHANIC DIES OF THE SAME ROOT CAUSE. 'One watches the map while the other digs' has value only if a warned human can win a detonation or evade one in time. They cannot, at 250ms versus 20ms. The stated viral loop evaporates the week the bots arrive.
legalFlags: A REGULATOR SEES AVIATOR. Stake $10, watch a multiplier climb, cash out before it blows up: that is the crash-game template (Bustabit 2016 → Aviator → dozens of Solana crash sites operating today, all licensed as casino games in every regulated market). Your only difference is that the crash is triggered by an opposing bot rather than an RNG — and from the player's epistemic position, an unpredictable exogenous event terminating an accumulating multiplier is functionally indistinguishable from chance. The brief's instinct ('regulators judge what a product functionally is') is right and understates how close the resemblance is.

MATERIAL-ELEMENT STATES ARE THE REAL EXPOSURE, NOT PREDOMINANCE STATES. Where the test is whether the outcome depends 'in a material degree' on chance rather than predominantly, another player's bot timing is neither your skill nor within your control. Geofencing the ~10 standard skill-gaming exclusion states plus Florida (Ch. 849 bars wagering on games of skill) is the floor, not the ceiling.

PrizePicks' ~$15M New York settlement is the right precedent and the right lesson: restructuring the product worked, relabeling it did not. Budget a multi-jurisdiction opinion before the paid season, not after it.

Age gating and responsible-gaming tooling are non-optional given the crash-game resemblance. And note the trap in your own thesis: if you ever run keeper bots yourself, the 'the operator's bot is first in the liquidation queue' suspicion this design exists to defuse becomes a consumer-fraud allegation rather than a vibe.
critique.priorArt: Two directly on-point precedents, both bad for the predator side. ALIEN WORLDS is the closest economic analogue: the simplest possible click-to-mine loop on WAX, top of DappRadar for years, captured completely by botnets — a single actor draining ~10% of daily TLM, captchas defeated, the team publicly unable to stop it, TLM down 99%+, and the 'users' revealed as bot wallets. Cave-In's loop is strictly MORE bot-friendly, because a liquidation race is the single most bot-optimized activity in crypto (human participation in DeFi liquidation is effectively zero). FOMO3D is the second: a last-buyer timer game whose winner took the pot by spamming high-gas transactions to congest blocks and lock competitors out — the exact shape of your detonation race, won by infrastructure rather than by play. On the money side, the fixed-prize-pool paid-entry structure is the DFS/Skillz pattern and is genuinely the soundest economy of the three concepts: E ≤ 0.88 × S holds, there is no faucet-to-payout link, and the Axie failure (SLP minted ~5x burned, ~18-19% monthly inflation, −99%) is structurally impossible here. That part is correct and it is the reason this one survives review.
critique.suggestedFix: Kill the latency race — it is the one element here that cannot be tuned away, and it takes the crew mechanic, the human-predator fantasy and the grudge retention loop with it. Replace instant first-to-land detonation with a BATCHED CLAIM WINDOW: when a shaft crosses integrity 1.00 it opens a 3-second window, every valid claim submitted inside that window enters a pool, and the winner is drawn from the pool via MagicBlock VRF (free, <50ms, inside the ER). Reaction time still gates ENTRY — noticing and acting within 3 seconds is a real human skill — but a 15ms bot and a 400ms human then have identical odds once both are in. Bots keep their breadth advantage across many shafts; humans can finally win the specific shaft they are watching, which is what the grudge loop and the crew mechanic actually require. Ship this alongside a SHORE retune (make integrity restored scale with depth, or price the cost by integrity restored rather than a flat 50×D) so the defensive verb is not dominated 500:1. Both are two-day changes, neither alters the product's identity, and that is why this is the one of the three I would actually run the 200-player season on.

name: Copycat
pitch: A 3-minute one-thumb survival game where every winning build is permanently named after the player who discovered it first — and you get paid a little every time someone else plays yours.
coreLoop: You drop into a 3-minute arena. One thumb, auto-attack, enemies swarm in waves. Every 30 seconds the game offers 3 relics from a pool of 60; you pick 1. Eight picks per run, so a run is an ordered path through a huge combination space. At 3:00 you either survive or die and post a Depth score (wave reached x survival time). Then the hook: instead of starting blind, you can load someone else's named Blueprint off the public board — 'Ash Spiral by @mina, 91,043 plays' — and run it. You get 5 free Copies a day. The 30-second unit is: die at wave 22, see the board, see a build 2 relics away from yours that nobody has claimed, run again. Discovery is the loop; the leaderboard is a list of people's names attached to ideas.
whyOnChain: Honest answer first: the game is completely fun with zero crypto, and I would ship it that way to 10,000 players before touching a chain. What crypto genuinely adds is the payout rail. Paying 5,000 people between $0.40 and $40 a week across 90 countries is economically impossible on Web2 rails — Roblox DevEx requires a $30 minimum, ID verification and a US-compatible bank; PayPal micropayments eat 30% at that ticket size. USDC to an embedded wallet with Kora paying fees makes a $0.40 weekly payout viable, which is what lets the creator economy reach the long tail instead of only the top 200. Second, smaller: the claim ledger is public and append-only, so 'who found it first' is not the studio's word against a player's. That matters the moment real money attaches to priority. Everything else — the sim, matchmaking, cosmetics — is better off-chain and I would not pretend otherwise.
solanaPrimitives: MagicBlock Ephemeral Rollup — the 3-minute run executes as a delegated session at ~10ms slots, Supersize-style (tx every ~30ms, lands ~50ms), so the score is authoritative rather than a client claim; 64KB ER txs let a whole run's input frames commit in one transaction at undelegation
MagicBlock VRF in-ER — free, <50ms, for the 3-relic offer roll every 30 seconds; never SlotHashes, since these rolls now have money attached
MagicBlock Session Keys — sign once at app open, play all day, no popup per run
Kora fee relayer (shipped April 2026) — players never hold SOL and never see a fee
Privy embedded wallet — created silently behind Apple/Google sign-in; the word 'wallet' never appears in the first session

Bubblegum V2 soulbound compressed NFTs — the Blueprint claim itself, non-transferable by design (~$500 per 1M assets vs $15-30k for Core accounts). Soulbound is deliberate: it kills the speculative market and with it most of the securities analysis
ZK Compression (Light Protocol) — per-player run history and progression records at ~1000x lower cost than standard accounts
Metaplex Core (mpl-core 1.10) — only for the small set of genuinely tradeable cosmetic skins, ~0.0029 SOL each
Solana Attestation Service — proof-of-uniqueness gating on Blueprint claims, as the anti-farming layer
DAS API (Helius/Triton) — hard dependency for reading the cNFT blueprint board; budget it
moneyFlow: IN: $4.99/mo Copycat Pass (Apple/Google IAP on mobile, card or USDC on web and the Solana dApp Store build where there is no 30% cut); rewarded video ads at ~$8-14 eCPM in tier-1 geos; cosmetic Core NFT skins at $2-$20. OUT: 25% of NET revenue (after store cut and ad-network cut) into a weekly Discoverer Pool, split by that week's copy-plays, paid in USDC, hard-capped at $200 per blueprint per week so a single viral build cannot eat the pool. NO NATIVE TOKEN — deliberately. There is no in-game currency at all, which means there is no faucet, no sink, and no emissions death spiral to design around; the 2026 record (95% average token drawdown, 97% of gaming token launches underperforming) says the token is the liability. The only 'sink' needed is the 5-Copies-per-day rate limit, which is an attention sink, not a currency one. Team earns 75% of net revenue, denominated in fiat and USDC, completely independent of any token price.
firstSession: 0:00 Install from App Store. Open. No sign-in, no wallet, no permission prompts — straight into a run. 0:08 First enemy wave, one thumb, no tutorial text. 0:30 First relic choice, 3 cards, 4 seconds on the clock. 3:00 You die at wave 22. Death screen shows: 'Closest Blueprint: Ash Spiral by @mina — 91,043 plays this week.' 3:20 Tap COPY. Second run with her build, you reach wave 31. 6:30 Third run, the game highlights 'this relic pair has never been claimed.' You die at wave 38, one wave short of the claim threshold. 7:00 Fourth run, you clear it. Modal: 'Name this build. Claiming takes 4 seconds.' 7:04 Apple sign-in. Privy creates the wallet in the background, Kora pays the fee, a Bubblegum V2 soulbound cNFT mints. You type 'Bramble Engine.' 7:10 It is on the public board with your handle on it. Nothing on screen has said blockchain, wallet, gas, or earn. Around day 3, once you have 4 blueprints with real play counts, the app shows a Discoverer tab with a dollar figure. That is the first and only time money is mentioned.
viralMechanic: Attribution is the payload. Every run played from a Blueprint puts the discoverer's handle on the HUD for the full 3 minutes and on the death screen. Copy counts are public and update live. The share asset is not 'come play my game' — it is 'I invented this, 91,000 people have played it.' That is a claim about the sharer, not about us, which is why it travels: it is the same mechanic that spreads Balatro seeds and TikTok sounds. Structurally, a player who wants their build played must recruit players who will play it, so growth is directly downstream of the thing the creator already wants. The payout amplifies it but does not create it — build attribution alone would spread this.
mvpScope: 2-4 weeks, web + PWA first, no native app: one arena, 24 relics (not 60), fixed 3-minute run, deterministic sim written once in Rust and compiled to both wasm (client prediction) and an ER program (authority), blueprint claim + public board, Privy embedded wallet + Kora gasless, weekly payouts run by a manual script off a CSV. CUTS: mobile native builds, ads, subscription, cosmetics, seasons, the anti-sybil attestation layer, DAS-backed board pagination (just read a Postgres mirror), and any leaderboard beyond a single global one. The MVP question is not 'do payouts work' — it is 'do players spend their fourth run hunting an unclaimed combination.' If they do not, no amount of USDC fixes it.
biggestRisk: The payout turns discovery into farming and the farming poisons the board. The combination space is enumerable; a bot farm will grind it, claim thousands of blueprints, and collect the long tail of the pool while real players find nothing left to name. This is Axie's scholarship problem in miniature — the moment an activity pays, someone industrializes it, and the industrialized version is not fun to be near. Mitigations (per-account claim cap of 20/season, Solana Attestation Service uniqueness proofs, requiring human-plausible input entropy in the ER-recorded frames) are all defeatable by a determined operator, and each one adds friction for honest players. Secondary risk: Google Play explicitly bans promoting or glamorizing earnings from play, so the Discoverer payout can never appear in a store listing, a screenshot, or an ad — which means the single most distinctive feature is invisible in the channel that drives installs.

critique.name: Copycat
technicalBlockers: ER unit economics invert the business at every scale. MagicBlock public-node pricing is 0.0003 SOL per ER session (charged at undelegation) + 0.0001 SOL per commit. At SOL≈$80 that is $0.024 + $0.008 = $0.032 per delegated run, minimum. The design's own loop is ~8 runs/day/DAU (own runs + 5 free Copies) = $0.256/day/DAU in settlement fees alone. A hybrid-casual mobile ARPDAU of $0.06 (generous: 2% conversion on a $4.99 sub after 30% store cut, plus 3 rewarded views at a $4 blended global eCPM) means MagicBlock fees are ~4.3x gross revenue. Even at ONE run per day it is $0.032 vs $0.06 — 53% of gross revenue before you pay a single Discoverer. The fix (delegate once per day, not per run) drops it to ~$0.024/day but leaves the player's account non-composable all day and still eats 40% of ARPDAU.

The 'authoritative rather than a client claim' premise does not survive the CU arithmetic. A bullet-heaven sim at 30Hz x 180s = 5,400 ticks. Even with spatial hashing and a hand-tuned Pinocchio inner loop, ~200 entities implies ~1,000 pair checks/tick at ~20 CU each plus integration and spawn logic — call it 30k CU/tick, i.e. ~162M CU per run. ER caps are 200k CU/instruction and 1.4M CU/tx, so replaying one run is ~116 transactions / ~810 instructions. The L1 settlement commit cannot verify any of it (12M CU per writable account per block, and the commit is a byte write, not a re-execution). So the ER is not proving the run — it is executing it as a trusted single non-voting sequencer whose fraud-proof and DA model the landscape explicitly lists as UNVERIFIED. You have replaced 'trust the studio' with 'trust MagicBlock', which is a downgrade for a product where money attaches to scores.

Runs are not wall-clock-bound in the ER. The 3-minute duration is enforced only by the client's frame pacing; the ER processes transactions as fast as they arrive, and a 64KB ER tx will happily carry thousands of input frames at once. A headless farm completes a 'three-minute run' in seconds. Every anti-abuse assumption in the design implicitly assumes 3 real minutes of wall clock per copy-play; none of that holds.

Blueprint scarcity collapses combinatorially. C(60,8) = 2,558,620,845 distinct unordered relic sets (ordered paths ≈ 1.07e14). At 100k DAU x 8 runs/day = 800k runs/day, essentially every run produces a never-before-seen set, so 'first discovery' is automatic rather than scarce and the board becomes millions of near-duplicate names — the exact discovery-collapse failure of Mario Maker and Dreams. Gate claims to only strong builds and the effective space collapses to the ~50-200 builds the metagame actually converges on, all of which are claimed permanently in week one, locking out every month-2 player. Neither fork is the pitched experience, and the pitch has no third option.

DAS-API is a hard dependency for reading the blueprint board (no getAccountInfo path for cNFTs), and Helius tiers run $499-999/mo plus $500-6,000/mo LaserStream add-ons post-April-2026 pricing. That is a $12k-$80k/yr line item against an MVP with zero revenue.
economicHoles: The Discoverer Pool pays dust at any realistic scale. 100k DAU, net revenue ≈ $43k/mo (2,000 subs at $4.99 less 30% store = $6,986; ads at $0.012/DAU/day = $36k), 25% = $10,750/mo ≈ $2,480/week. Copy-plays at 5/day/DAU = 3.5M/week. That is $0.00071 per copy-play. The pitch's own hero example (@mina, 91,043 plays) earns $64.60/week — the $200 cap never binds — and the long tail the entire USDC rail was justified by earns 1.4 cents for 20 plays. The stated goal of 'paying 5,000 people $0.40 to $40 a week' needs $2k-$200k/week, so the low end alone consumes the entire pool at 100k DAU. The payout rail is a problem you only have at 500k+ DAU, i.e. after you already have a hit.

The sybil attack is copy-play farming, not claim farming, and the gasless stack makes it free to the attacker and expensive to you. Privy wallets are created silently, Kora sponsors L1 fees, ER gameplay txs are 0 SOL, and runs are not wall-clock-bound. Attacker marginal cost per fake copy-play ≈ $0. Studio marginal cost ≈ $0.032 (ER session + commit). A farm generating 1M fake copy-plays/day costs YOU $32,000/day while draining a $354/day pool. This is an unbounded griefing vector that works even if the farmer never collects a cent — you have built a service that pays MagicBlock $0.032 every time an anonymous stranger asks you to.

Alien Worlds is the settled precedent and the numbers are public: ~170k daily active miners of which Naavik estimated 30-45% were bots (HAW/DAW ratio ~47%, implying >11h/day play), with TLM down >50% in 2022. Every 'the activity pays, so someone industrialises it' design lands here. The proposed mitigations do not survive contact: a 20-claims/season cap is defeated by more accounts; Solana Attestation Service uniqueness via Civic costs roughly $0.20-1.00 per verification and inserts an identity step into a product whose entire first-session pitch is 'no sign-in, no wallet, no permission prompts'.

No in-game currency is genuinely the right call and removes the emissions death spiral — credit where due. But it also means the only thing you can pay out is real revenue, and 25% of net revenue is a permanent 25% haircut on unit economics in a category (hybrid-casual) where paid UA already runs at LTV/CAC margins under 1.3. Handing a quarter of net to non-paying users while buying installs at $2-4 CPI is a structurally unprofitable growth loop.

The pitch's Web2-rails premise is factually wrong in a way that makes its own argument stronger, so fix the citation: Roblox DevEx requires 30,000 Earned Robux (~$105), not $30, at an effective 26.6% share. But Tipalti/Wise/PayPal Payouts do sub-dollar global payouts today at $0.20-1.00 per transfer, which is fine at $40/week and absurd at $0.40/week — and at $0.40/week the payout is below the psychological threshold where anyone changes behaviour, which is the actual reason the rail does not matter.
legalFlags: Google Play prohibits promoting or glamorising earnings from play. The pitch acknowledges this but under-reads the consequence: you cannot put the Discoverer payout in the store listing, screenshots, ASO, or UA creative, which means you can never A/B test whether the payout drives retention in your main acquisition channel. You will spend 25% of net revenue on a feature whose lift you are legally barred from measuring where it matters.

Apple 3.1.1 (IAP), 3.1.5(b) (crypto/NFT restrictions — apps may not unlock features via mechanisms other than IAP, and NFT-gated functionality is restricted) and the real-money-gaming rules all touch this. Minting a soulbound cNFT for free gameplay is probably survivable; a 'Discoverer' tab showing a dollar figure is not obviously so, and review outcomes here are inconsistent enough that you should assume a rejection cycle.

US payor obligations: W-9 collection and 1099-NEC/1099-MISC for any payee crossing $600/yr. At the pitched distribution the top blueprints cross it immediately, so you need a tax-ops vendor and a payee-onboarding flow — which reintroduces exactly the KYC friction the USDC rail was supposed to avoid, for precisely the users who earn enough to matter.

Paying users USDC from a studio-controlled treasury on a recurring schedule is a payout, not transmission, so MSB exposure is low — but only if you never let players send value to each other. Do not add trading, gifting, or a marketplace for the payout balance without a fresh opinion.
critique.priorArt: No prior art found for named build-attribution with royalties specifically — that combination appears genuinely novel, and the free version of it (Balatro seed sharing, Slay the Spire, Trackmania) demonstrably spreads. The adjacent precedents all failed in instructive ways: Roblox Creator Rewards (2024) pays by engagement time and works only at Roblox scale with a 26.6% share and a ~$105 cash-out floor; Mario Maker and Dreams established that UGC discovery collapses without editorial curation; Alien Worlds (WAX) is the canonical pay-per-action outcome (30-45% bots of ~170k daily miners per Naavik, TLM -50% in 2022). On Solana in 2026 the live comparables are Infinite Royale (kill-to-earn USDC per elimination) and Sprout's Pollinators event, whose prize pool was $400 USDC split across the top 50 — $8 a head. That is the actual scale of Solana game payouts today, and it is two orders of magnitude below the pitch's assumption.
critique.suggestedFix: Delete the ephemeral rollup and the per-play payout, and make Blueprints artificially scarce and seasonal. Run the sim on a normal authoritative server (you already trust a single sequencer either way, and $0.032/run buys nothing you cannot get from a $200/mo game server), keep only the claim ledger on-chain since that is the one thing the pitch correctly identifies as needing an append-only public record. Replace 'anyone can claim any novel set' with a curated weekly frontier of ~200 designer-seeded unclaimed relic pairs that resets each season — this restores scarcity, gives month-6 players something to discover, and caps claims at a number a human editor can moderate. Replace pay-per-copy-play with a fixed weekly purse to the top ~200 blueprints ranked by unique attested players, which makes the farm's marginal revenue zero regardless of how many fake sessions it generates. Then ship it free to 10,000 players exactly as the pitch says, and only wire up USDC once you observe the fourth-run-hunting behaviour the MVP is actually testing for.

name: Hunch
pitch: Ten yes-or-no questions about the next 48 hours. Swipe. Beat the 29 other people in your league. Free, forever, no money down.
coreLoop: Once a day, at a time you choose, 10 cards appear. Each is a claim resolving within 48 hours: 'Manchester City wins Saturday.' 'Bitcoin closes above $95k Friday.' 'It rains in Lagos tomorrow.' Swipe right for yes, left for no — and how far you swipe sets your confidence, 51% to 99%. The whole set takes 70-90 seconds. Scoring is Brier: confident and right pays big, confident and wrong hurts badly, and hedging at 55% barely moves you either way. That single design choice is what makes it a game rather than a quiz — you are managing conviction, not knowledge. Then the drip: cards resolve throughout the next two days, each one a push notification with a point swing. You are not waiting for one result, you are getting eight small verdicts spread across 48 hours. Weekly, your league of 30 reshuffles: top 7 promote, bottom 7 relegate, ten tiers deep. Duolingo's exact structure, because it is the most proven retention mechanic in casual mobile.
whyOnChain: Mostly nothing, for the game itself. Hunch is a Web2 game with a wallet and I will say that plainly — the swiping, the scoring, the leagues, the streaks all work on Postgres. Crypto earns its place in exactly two places, both outside the loop. First, the credential: a forecasting track record is only worth something if nobody can edit it, including us. 'Top 4% calibrated over 2,300 forecasts, timestamped, verifiable by anyone' is a real portable asset — the Solana Attestation Service plus a per-player commit makes it checkable by a third party who does not trust our servers, which is the whole point of a credential. A studio-hosted score is a vanity number. Second, the payout: sponsor-funded weekly prizes of $2-$40 to thousands of winners across 100 countries is a rail problem Web2 cannot price. If you removed both, you would still have the game — which is exactly the test the 2026 graveyard says to apply, and Hunch passes it.
solanaPrimitives: Switchboard On-Demand custom feed definitions — the research is explicit that Switchboard's arbitrary-API feeds are the right fit for NON-price game oracles; sports results, election calls, weather, box office, all resolve here (crate 0.13.0, npm 3.10.6, actively maintained)

3-of-5 human resolver committee with a 12-hour dispute window on-chain — the fallback for ambiguously-worded questions, because a badly-worded card that resolves wrong is the fastest way to lose a forecasting community
Solana Attestation Service — the calibration credential itself, issued per season, readable by any third party
ZK Compression (Light Protocol) — a player accumulates ~2,000 forecast records; compressed accounts at ~1000x lower cost make lifetime history economically storable on-chain
Kora fee relayer — the daily answer commit is gasless and the player never holds SOL
Privy embedded wallet — created invisibly on day 3, behind an Apple or email sign-in
Metaplex Core — league tier badges as collectibles, ~0.0029 SOL each, cosmetic only
Solana L1 only, no rollup — a once-daily commit needs 350ms slots, not 10ms ones. Per-player PDAs mean local fee markets keep priority fees near zero (there is no hot global account to contend on)
USDC for all prize payouts; no native token at any point
moneyFlow: IN: brand-sponsored question packs (a football club, a studio, an exchange pays to place a 3-card set — this is native advertising that people actually want to interact with); $3.99/mo Pro (second daily set, full history export, calibration analytics, no ads); rewarded video for a streak freeze. OUT: a FIXED weekly prize pool, sized as a contractual line item from sponsorship revenue, split across the top leagues in USDC. The critical structure: there is NO ENTRY FEE, EVER, and no deposits are ever accepted. Prizes are funded from revenue, never from a player pot. That removes the consideration element of the consideration+chance+prize test entirely, which is the difference between a game and a regulated gambling product. There is no in-game currency, no dual-currency system, and nothing that simulates casino or lottery content — the 2026 sweepstakes bans in NY, LA, OK, IN, IA, ME, TN all target 'dual- or multi-currency systems simulating lottery or casino-style gaming,' and Hunch has neither currency nor casino content. Team earns the sponsorship and subscription margin. Nothing about the business depends on a token price.
firstSession: 0:00 Open. No sign-in, no wallet, no onboarding carousel. First card is already on screen: 'The Fed cuts rates on Sept 17.' 0:08 You swipe right, halfway — 68% confident. Haptic tick. 0:20 Card 4 is a football result, you swipe hard left, 91%. 1:15 Ten cards done. 'You're in Bronze League IV. 30 players. Resolves Sunday.' You see 29 handles and where you sit. 1:30 'Come back tomorrow. Cards 2, 5 and 9 resolve tonight.' App closes. 18:40 Push: 'Card 3 resolved. You called it at 91%. +18. You're 6th.' You open, look, close — 12 seconds. That short re-open is the actual retention engine. Day 2: same 90 seconds, plus a streak counter at 2. Day 3, after your first correct high-confidence call: 'Your record is public and permanent. Claim it?' → Apple sign-in, wallet created invisibly, Kora pays, an attestation is written. The screen says 'your record' and never says wallet, chain, or token. Money is not mentioned in the first week at all.
viralMechanic: Verifiable I-told-you-so. Every resolved card generates a share card carrying your pre-commit timestamp and its on-chain proof link — evidence that you called it BEFORE it happened. Unverifiable hindsight bragging is one of the internet's largest activities and it is currently worthless because anyone can claim it; a cryptographic timestamp converts it into something people will actually argue with. Player A shares because being right in public is the reward, and player B clicks because the natural response to someone claiming a call is to test whether you would have made it. Secondary and stronger for retention: leagues are 30 real people who see your handle every day, and Duolingo has demonstrated that relegation anxiety among 30 strangers outperforms almost every social feature ever shipped.
mvpScope: 2-4 weeks: 10 hand-curated questions a day written by one editor (zero oracle automation — a human resolves everything for the first two months, which is faster, cheaper, and higher-quality than a Switchboard integration you have not tested), Brier scoring, 30-player leagues with promote/relegate, streaks, push notifications on resolution, and a single on-chain compressed commit per player per day so the timestamp claim is true from day one. NO PRIZES AT ALL in v1 — this is the point of the MVP. Measure D7 and D30 with zero money in the system. CUTS: Switchboard automation, the resolver committee, the attestation credential, sponsorships, Pro tier, prize pools, and every payment rail. If a free forecasting league does not hold 20%+ D7 on its own, adding money will buy farmers, not players, and the correct decision is to kill it.
biggestRisk: It only retains for the ~200k people who already enjoy Metaculus and Polymarket, and for a genuinely mass-market user, swiping on claims about the Fed is homework. The 'fun' here is thin and intellectual — there is no dexterity, no build, no thing you make. That is the real risk and I do not have a confident answer to it; the MVP exists specifically to fail fast on it. The second risk is regulatory and it is severe: the moment prizes attach to real-world event outcomes, state gaming regulators look at what the product functionally IS, not what you call it. PrizePicks paid ~$15M to the NY Gaming Commission and exited the state for exactly this misjudgment, and got C&Ds in FL, AR, MI and MA. Free entry is a genuine legal difference, not a fig leaf — but 'genuine legal difference' still costs a six-figure multi-jurisdiction opinion and a geofence, and the Kalshi preemption shelter (3rd Cir., Apr 2026) attaches only to CFTC DCM registration, which a small team cannot buy.

critique.name: Hunch
technicalBlockers: The architecture is correctly sized and I am not going to invent a problem here: one commit per player per day on L1 with per-player PDAs is the right call. 100k DAU x 5,000 lamports = 0.5 SOL/day ≈ $40/day ≈ $14.6k/yr in signature fees, plus a compressed-state write at ~100-150k CU which at 10k microlamports/CU is ~$0.00012. Local fee markets keep priority fees at zero because there is no hot global account. Declining the ephemeral rollup for a once-daily commit is the single best technical decision across all three concepts.

The commit/reveal design is unspecified and both obvious choices break the product. Plaintext on-chain: every player reads the top forecaster's answers before resolution and copies them, and a 30-person league becomes 30 copies of one person inside a week. Hashed commits: losers simply never reveal — the exact failure Switchboard's own docs warn about ('take collateral at commit time, not reveal time') — and you cannot take collateral because the whole legal shield is that there is no entry fee. Scoring unrevealed forecasts as maximally wrong punishes the casual who forgot to open the app, destroying the retention the design is built on. The only workable model is studio-custodied plaintext with an on-chain hash and unconditional studio-published reveals at resolution, which works cryptographically but must be designed deliberately, not assumed.

The credential — the primary stated crypto justification — is not actually trustless, and this is the load-bearing flaw. The studio writes the 10 questions, chooses the resolution source, words the resolution criteria, and operates the resolver committee. 'Top 4% calibrated over 2,300 forecasts' therefore means 'top 4% among people answering questions Hunch wrote and Hunch graded.' A third party who does not trust your servers still has to trust your question selection and your grading, so the attestation proves timestamping and nothing about validity. An on-chain commit converts an unfalsifiable brag into a timestamped brag, which is real but much smaller than 'portable verifiable credential'.

ZK Compression storage is fine but the indexer is not free: ~2,000 records/player x 100k players = 200M compressed accounts, all of which require a Photon/DAS-class indexer to read. Helius $499-999/mo plus LaserStream $500-6,000/mo puts this at $12k-$80k/yr against an MVP that by design has zero revenue.
