EVERY LEGAL ACTION BURNS THE RESOURCE THE GAME IS ABOUT, SO THE RESOURCE ISN'T PLAYABLE. The pitch says anonymity is spent 'one revelation at a time, across six weeks,' with ~6 reveals to identification. But announcements are public and binding. If only ~15 of 120 predicates are worth 14, and a 14-point predicate is by construction held by a small fraction of seats — say 0.5% of 50,000 = 250 — then ONE truthful high announcement cuts the candidate field from 50,000 to a few hundred, and a second cuts it to single digits. Truth narrows you. Lying, if called, permanently and publicly attaches the predicate. The only non-leaking line is to announce low values every hand, which forfeits every hand. There is no strategy that preserves the resource, which means the resource is not a resource, it is a countdown. Anonymity is gone in two or three twelve-minute games, not thirty — and the season is six weeks long with a Seat locked to a wallet you cannot re-roll without another 180-day-aged address.

THE HIDDEN-VERIFICATION FIX BREAKS THE PUNISHMENT. You can verify a Merkle proof privately inside the TEE and publish only a boolean, which stops honest proofs from leaking. But then 'the predicate they falsely claimed is publicly and permanently attached to their Seat' has no verifiable basis to publish either, and the punishment that makes bluffing costly disappears. Revelation-to-verify and non-revelation-as-resource are in direct structural contradiction.

F2P COSMETICS CANNOT CARRY A SIX-FIGURE FIXED COST IN THIS CATEGORY. Cosmetic-only ARPU in a niche crypto title is realistically $0.50–$2 per MAU. Against a $60k–$360k/year data pipeline plus Private ER plus staff, you need tens of thousands of engaged MAU for a five-player bluffing game with a deliberately invasive onboarding screen, in a market where 93% of web3 titles are dead and funding fell to $73M in a quarter. Photo Finish LIVE — the best-performing Solana game economy on record at $23M horse sales and $50M race fees cumulative — did not clear $100M revenue in 2025. Your comparable is far below that and has no cash-out to sell.
legalFlags: THIS IS A TARGETING TOOL FOR VIOLENT CRIME AND THAT IS THE FINDING THAT SHOULD STOP IT. CertiK documented 52 verified crypto 'wrench attacks' in H1 2026, up 33% YoY; home invasions went from 1 in H1 2025 to 20 in H1 2026; kidnappings 12 → 16; ~$101M in claimed losses; Europe was 75% of incidents. Chainalysis and CoinDesk report the category up ~75% in 2026. Attackers select targets using leaked databases, social profiles and BLOCKCHAIN ACTIVITY. Rap Sheet's explicit growth loop is 'import addresses you already know,' its stated most-satisfying win is 'unmasking a rival Seat as someone you actually know,' and it awards points for holdings ('has never once sold at a loss,' 'held through a >60% drawdown') that read as a wealth-and-conviction screen. You are gamifying and incentivizing exactly the reconnaissance step of the fastest-growing violent crime in this industry. No opt-in toggle or copy change addresses this.

YOU WOULD BE VOLUNTARILY ASSEMBLING THE MOST ATTRACTIVE WRENCH-ATTACK DATABASE IN EXISTENCE. The registration flow requires binding a real, 180-day-old wallet, and SAS attestation ties one Seat to one attested human. The resulting table maps attested identity → real wallet → 120 behavioral and wealth predicates, for every player. The TEE protects it from opponents, not from the indexer that must compute it, not from the operator who provisions the enclave, and not from a breach. crypto.news reported in 2026 that leaked SHIPPING ADDRESSES were sufficient to fuel this attack class; you would be holding something categorically richer.

GDPR / EDPB 02/2025 v2.0 (adopted 7 July 2026). On-chain data linkable to a natural person is personal data. The guidelines state technical impossibility cannot justify non-compliance with erasure, and recommend not registering cleartext, encrypted OR hashed personal data on-chain. Rap Sheet writes soulbound, permanent Perjury marks and predicate attributions on-chain by design; erasure is structurally impossible and soulbinding makes it more so. Article 22 automated-profiling exposure is direct. Worse, several predicates process data about THIRD PARTIES who are not players and cannot consent — 'transacted in the same block as a wallet that later did >$1M volume' processes the whale's data too. There is no available lawful basis for a product whose stated purpose is enabling users to identify other data subjects.

APP STORE REJECTION IS LIKELY. Permanent public 'Perjury' marks naming users are user-visible reputational content; Apple 1.2 requires filtering and removal mechanisms for objectionable UGC and Google Play's harassment policy covers doxxing outright. A product that rewards de-anonymizing people will not clear either review. The Solana dApp Store (0% fee, 1,561 apps) is the escape hatch and its addressable base is ~200k Seekers.

Defamation and harassment exposure from permanent, public, mockable accusations attached to identities the game itself is designed to link to real people. Free-to-play removes the gambling analysis cleanly — that judgment was correct — but it removes the smallest of this concept's legal problems.
critique.priorArt: The share-hook half has been tried repeatedly and works; the game half has not been tried and the doxxing half has been tried and is the most-criticized product in the sector. DegenScore Beacon (soulbound reputation NFT from on-chain DeFi activity) and Nomis (multichain on-chain reputation protocol, still operating, still B2B) both proved wallet-derived scores are computable and mildly interesting — and neither ever became a consumer game or a retention product. Zerion and Coinbase wallet 'wrapped' recaps proved the reveal screen generates shares; they also proved it generates one share and zero retention, which is precisely the wrong shape for the pitch's claim that this is 'the marketing and the retention hook.' Arkham Intelligence is the closest analogue to the actual loop — paid bounties for de-anonymizing wallets — and it drew sustained industry criticism as a doxxing marketplace. The hidden-information technology is real and improving (TEE and FHE onchain card games shipped in 2026), so the mechanism is buildable. Nobody has built wallet-history-as-a-card-game, and after the 2026 wrench-attack numbers I do not think that is an oversight.
critique.suggestedFix: Keep the bluffing mechanic; replace the dataset. The genuinely good idea here is 'bluff with cards that are verifiably true and can be challenged' — a challenge-and-prove loop where non-holders literally cannot produce a proof is elegant and CU-cheap. What is fatal is that the cards are real people's financial history and the win condition is unmasking them. Derive predicates from IN-GAME history instead: a Seat accumulates verifiable, challengeable facts about how it has PLAYED — 'has bluffed a 14 and been called,' 'has never folded to a challenge,' 'won a table holding no card above 4.' These are on-chain, unforgeable, retroactively unfakeable, adversarially readable, and time-gated exactly like the wallet predicates, so every whyOnChain argument survives intact — but they are generated by consenting participants inside your own game, so GDPR, the wrench-attack surface, the app-store rejection, the boring-wallet risk, the $30k/month warehouse, and the pay-to-have-been-early unfairness all disappear at once. Season one bootstraps from a small opt-in set of coarse wallet facts with no third-party references. Run the author's own three-day test first — generate 10,000 real Rap Sheets and read them — but read them for whether they are SAFE to publish, not only whether they are funny.

name: Fuse
pitch: A 20-second countdown where the bomb isn't random — every other player secretly planted one, and you have to cash out before someone else's goes off.
coreLoop: 16-player lobby, ~30 seconds end to end. Phase 1 (10s): you secretly plant a fuse — one integer from 101 to 1000, meaning a multiplier between 1.01x and 10.00x — and stake 0.02 SOL. Phase 2 (~18s): a single giant number ticks up from 1.00x, +0.01 every ~20ms, and 16 dots on screen wink out as people cash out. The round ends the instant the multiplier crosses the LOWEST fuse belonging to a player who hasn't cashed out yet. You press SPACE to cash out. Scoring is pari-mutuel: each cashed-out player earns points equal to their cashout multiplier; the player whose fuse detonated earns 2x their fuse value; everyone still alive at detonation earns zero. The 0.32 SOL pot minus a 5% rake is split pro-rata by points. The math means panic-cashing at 1.02x actually LOSES money (0.0117 SOL back on a 0.02 stake in a typical round), while planting a fuse the crowd walks into pays ~2.7x. The timid play is punished by construction, so nobody plays timid, so the tension never decays. There is zero randomness anywhere in the game.
whyOnChain: Three things break in Web2. (1) The entire game is hidden information about other players' commitments — a Web2 server knows every fuse and could nudge one lobby's outcome and nobody could ever detect it. Here the fuses are hash-committed on L1 with collateral taken at commit time (per Switchboard's own commit-reveal rule), and after the round every fuse and nonce is published, so any player can replay the round and verify the detonation order. In a game whose only content is 'did I get read', a provably unrigged referee is the product. (2) Pari-mutuel settlement with no operator custody — the pot is a PDA, payouts are a deterministic function of revealed commits, and I never hold player money. (3) Global, instant, sub-cent settlement in 20-second rounds; no payment processor on earth will settle 90 rounds an hour at $1.60 stakes. What crypto does NOT add: the mechanic itself would be fun as a free browser game with fake points, and I'd say so — but the honest version of this game is a wager, and the wager is what makes people read each other seriously.
solanaPrimitives: MagicBlock Ephemeral Rollup (ephemeral-rollups-sdk 0.16.2) — the 18-second tick loop runs at ~10ms slots with ~30ms send / ~50ms land, the Supersize.gg profile; 16 player PDAs + one match PDA are delegated at lobby open and undelegated at settle

MagicBlock Private ER (TEE-backed) — holds revealed fuses during the live round so the sequencer can answer 'has any un-cashed fuse tripped' without leaking the ordering to spectators; MVP ships without PER using plain commit-reveal and a disclosed trusted sequencer
MagicBlock Session Keys (useSessionKeyManager) — sign once when you join the lobby, then cash out with a keypress, no wallet popup mid-round
Kora fee relayer (Solana Foundation, shipped Apr 2026) — gas sponsored so a player's only SOL outlay is their stake
Wallet Standard discovery via @solana/kit-plugin-wallet with @solana/kit 7.1.1 — the CT audience already has Phantom/Backpack; no embedded-wallet detour
MagicBlock ER pricing — 0 SOL per ER tx, 0.0003 SOL per session at undelegation, 0.0001 SOL per L1 commit; a full 16-player round settles for well under a cent
Deliberately NO VRF and NO SlotHashes — the absence of any chance element is a legal design decision, not an oversight
Anchor 1.1.2 (@anchor-lang/core), Pinocchio 0.11.2 for the per-tick ER handler, Mollusk 0.15.0 in CI to catch CU regressions
moneyFlow: IN: 0.02 SOL stake per player per round, staked at commit. OUT: 95% of the pot redistributed to that same round's players pro-rata by points; the 5% house rake (0.016 SOL ≈ $1.28/round at SOL $80) is the only revenue. SINKS: the rake is the sink — it is a pure fee on a zero-sum transfer, not an emission. There is no token, no emission, no yield, no treasury, no staking, nothing to inflate. Nothing enters that a player did not put in that round; nothing leaves except the rake. Unit math: one lobby cycles ~90 rounds/hour = ~$115/hr; 10 concurrent lobbies = ~$1,150/hr at full utilization, which is a real solo-dev business at a few hundred concurrent players. Rent: match PDAs are closed and their rent-exemption deposit reclaimed at settle. Costs: MagicBlock session + commit fees (~0.0004 SOL/round), one Helius tier ($49–499/mo), a domain. No token launch, ever.
firstSession: 0:00 — CT post links to fuse.gg. Page shows a live round already running: a huge white number climbing on black, 16 dots, and a feed of the last 10 detonations ('anon planted 1.42x, blew up 11 players, took 0.19 SOL'). No wallet needed to watch. 0:20 — you watch two full rounds as a spectator. This is the hook; the game is legible in 20 seconds with no tutorial. 0:45 — 'JOIN NEXT ROUND' → Wallet Standard picker → Phantom connect → one signature that both approves the 0.02 SOL stake and provisions a session key scoped to the match program for the next hour. Kora sponsors gas, so you never see a SOL-for-fees error. 1:10 — lobby: a slider from 1.01x to 10.00x, one line of text ('the round ends the moment the number passes the lowest fuse still in play'), a 10-second timer. You plant at 2.00x because it's round, like everyone's first fuse. 1:25 — the number climbs, dots start winking out at 1.3x, 1.6x; you panic and cash at 1.71x. 1:26 — the round ends at 1.88x on someone else's fuse; you got 0.0198 SOL back, a small loss, and the postgame screen shows all 16 fuses: three people planted at 2.00x exactly, which is why 2.00x is a bad fuse. You have now learned the entire meta. 1:50 — you join the next round.
viralMechanic: The postgame screen is a shareable, single-image artifact: 16 fuse positions on a number line, the detonation point, and one line — 'anon.sol planted at 1.42x and ended it for 11 people, +0.19 SOL.' Detonating is the flex, and detonating is the highest-EV play, so the profitable move and the postable move are the same move. That's structural, not marketing. Second loop: because instant cash-outs LOSE money, every round produces at least one person who held too long, and 'held to 4.2x and got fused at 4.19x' is a better post than winning. Third: spectating requires no wallet and no install, so a quoted screenshot converts directly into a viewer, and viewers watch two rounds before they can help themselves. There are no referral codes and no points program — the research is unambiguous that points-to-token farming imports mercenaries and, per the SEC's March 2026 joint interpretation, 'recipients perform services' airdrops are not in the safe harbor teams assume.
mvpScope: 5 weeks solo. IN: one Anchor program (commit, reveal, tick, cashout, settle) with the tick handler written in Pinocchio for CU headroom; delegation/undelegation via ephemeral-rollups-sdk; one lobby size (16) at one stake (0.02 SOL); a ~600-line client — a number, 16 divs, a slider, and a WebSocket to the ER; commit-reveal with the ER sequencer trusted and that trust disclosed on the landing page in plain English; LiteSVM tests for the payoff function and Mollusk CU benchmarks in CI; Surfpool for local integration. CUT: Private ER / TEE (v2), multiple stake tiers, ranked ladder, any account system beyond the wallet, mobile app (mobile web only), chat, tournaments, cosmetics, replays beyond the last 50 rounds, any analytics beyond a Helius webhook writing settlements to SQLite. Week 1 payoff math + LiteSVM harness; weeks 2–3 program + ER delegation; week 4 client; week 5 devnet with 20 friends, then mainnet with a geofence and a $0.10 stake tier for the first weekend.
biggestRisk: Gambling law, and it is not close. This is a real-money contest with consideration and a prize, and the fact that I engineered out every source of chance is a genuinely strong argument in predominance-test states and a weak one in material-element states — where 'chance being material' can include variance in who else joined your lobby, and that argument has not been tested for a game shaped like this. Florida bars wagering on skill games by statute regardless. So the real MVP includes compliance-grade geolocation, an excluded-state list modeled on Skillz's, age gating, and — before any mainnet stake above a token amount — actual gaming counsel, which the research prices at $50k–$250k for a real multi-jurisdiction opinion. That is more than a solo dev's entire budget, which means the honest launch path is: ship free-to-play with fake points to prove the mechanic is fun and get the CT moment, THEN decide whether the wagering version is worth financing counsel for. Secondary risk, and it is serious: the MagicBlock ER trust model is explicitly UNVERIFIED — fraud proofs, data availability, and undelegation-under-validator-failure are not answered in public docs. I would be routing player stakes through a sequencer whose failure mode I cannot describe. Before mainnet I ask MagicBlock directly and build an L1 escape hatch that lets any player force-undelegate and reclaim their stake after a timeout, or I don't ship the real-money version.

critique.name: Fuse
technicalBlockers: THE PAYOFF MATRIX IS DEGENERATE — this is the whole review. Round ends at the lowest un-cashed fuse; detonator earns 2x their fuse. Symmetric play is never an equilibrium: if all 16 plant f and hold, each gets 2f points, ties 16 ways, and takes 0.304/16 = 0.019 SOL on a 0.02 stake (-5%). Deviate by ONE TICK to f-0.01 and you alone detonate; nobody else has cashed out, so Sum(points) = 2(f-0.01), all of it yours, and you take 100% of the 0.304 SOL pool = 15.2x on a 0.02 stake. Undercutting by 0.01 pays 15x. This is Bertrand / lowest-unique-bid and it iterates straight to the 1.01 floor.

At the floor the game does not exist. Detonation at 1.01 happens on the FIRST 20ms tick. No one can cash out below 1.01, so every non-detonator scores exactly 0. The climbing number, the 18-second phase 2, the 16 dots winking out, the SPACE bar — all of it is off-equilibrium content that will never render after week one.

Mixed-equilibrium arithmetic: a floor-planter's EV is 0.304 * E[1/(1+Binom(15,p))]. Setting that equal to the 0.02 stake requires E[1/(1+K)] = 0.0658, i.e. K ~ 14.2, i.e. p ~ 0.95. In equilibrium ~95% of the table plants at or within one tick of 1.01. The median round lasts 20 milliseconds.

Day-one bot extraction needs no latency edge and no sybils: one bot plants 101 (1.01x) and holds, every round. Against a human population planting 1.5-3.0 it is uniquely lowest essentially always and captures the full 0.304 SOL for a 0.02 stake. At 90 rounds/hr that is +25.6 SOL/hr = ~$2,048/hr at SOL $80. The game is drained before the CT thread finishes.

Latency vs. decision resolution. The multiplier grows 0.01/20ms = 0.5x per second. Human reaction to a changing numeral is ~250ms = 0.125x of drift; their own quoted send/land is 30ms/50ms = another 0.025x. Total ~0.15x of noise on a variable whose strategic granularity is 0.01x. Skill resolution is 15x coarser than the decision variable, and a co-located bot holds a permanent ~0.15x edge over every human, every round.

The referee IS the trusted party the pitch claims to eliminate. Whether your cashout landed before detonation is decided by ER intra-slot ordering at ~10ms, and MagicBlock's own docs explicitly warn against depending on slot timing. Their own landscape doc lists ER fraud proofs, data availability, and undelegation-under-validator-failure as UNVERIFIED. 'A provably unrigged referee is the product' and 'the referee is an undocumented single sequencer' cannot both be true.

Cold start is structural, not a marketing problem. The mechanic needs 16 simultaneous real-money players per 30-second cycle. Below ~8 the min-of-n undercutting gets sharper and the pot smaller. There is no house-bot backfill that does not reintroduce exactly the rigging the game exists to rule out.

Throughput is NOT the constraint (17 accounts/round is well under the 64-lock cap; the multiplier is a pure function of elapsed time and needs no per-tick tx). Lifecycle is: 10 lobbies * 90 rounds/hr * 17 PDAs * 2 (create+close) = ~30,600 L1 signatures/hr = ~8.5 TPS of pure overhead, ~0.153 SOL/hr in base fees, dev-paid via Kora. Plus a hardened landing layer (stale blockhash, CU budget, fee pricing, retry idempotency) is mandatory because a dropped cashout tx means a player loses money — their own landscape doc flags this as dedicated engineering. 5 weeks solo is not credible.
economicHoles: Sybil, if the floor exploit were somehow patched: 16 anonymous seats, no identity layer, no attestation. Take 8 of 16 seats for 0.16 SOL, plant all 8 at the floor, honest players score 0, you collect 0.304 SOL of which 0.16 was your own money. Net +0.144 SOL/round = +13 SOL/hr = ~$1,036/hr. Nothing in the design prevents lobby stacking.

5% rake against a 12-year market standard of 1%. bustabit has run since 2014 at a 1% edge and every degen knows that number. Fuse's player EV is -0.001 SOL/round; at 90-120 rounds/hr that is -0.09 to -0.12 SOL/hr = $7.20-$9.60/hr at SOL $80. A $100 bankroll has a ~10-hour expected life and, with variance, most players bust in 2-4. You are charging 5x the reference rake with a worse fairness story.

The revenue thesis requires being a top-1 Solana game. $1,150/hr needs 160 concurrent real-money players sustained. Star Atlas SAGE — AAA-funded, years of runway — is at ~750 DAU in Q2 2026. At a typical 2-5% CCU/DAU ratio, 160 CCU implies 3,000-8,000 DAU. Supersize.gg, the flagship reference for exactly this ER real-time stack, publishes no DAU at all.

Zero-sum-minus-rake with no sink other than the rake means there is no economy to design and no reason to be there except the wager. The pitch concedes this, then proposes shipping free-to-play with fake points as the compliant fallback — which deletes the entire whyOnChain. A points game with no money is 300 lines of Node and has no reason to touch Solana.
legalFlags: Pari-mutuel from entry fees is the single worst available structure. Florida's skill-game carve-out requires that the prize NOT be composed of entry fees, NOT vary with entry fees collected, and BE announced in advance. Fuse fails all three prongs simultaneously and by design, and Florida bars wagering on skill contests by statute. That is 22M people.

~12 states exclude cash entry on the Skillz model (AZ, AR, CT, DE, IN, IA, LA, ME, MT, SC, SD, TN). Skillz spent years and millions building that compliance stack and its equity still collapsed ~99% from the 2021 peak — that is the ceiling of the licensed skill-wagering category, not the floor.

'Zero randomness' is a strong predominance-test argument and a weak material-element argument. From your seat, WHO joined your anonymous 16-player lobby and WHAT they planted is pure chance and is the only thing determining your outcome. That is closer to a lottery than to chess, and it is untested for this shape of game.

Pari-mutuel wagering is a separately licensed category in most US states (racing commissions, Interstate Horseracing Act). Operating pooled-stakes betting outside racing is generally prohibited regardless of the skill analysis.

A 5% rake to a dev-controlled wallet is unambiguously operating a gambling business for profit. A solo operator escapes 18 U.S.C. 1955 (needs 5+ persons) but not state law, and the practical enforcement points are the domain registrar and any fiat on-ramp. Their own $50k-$250k counsel estimate exceeds the entire solo-dev budget, which they concede.
critique.priorArt: Extensive and unflattering. Crash games trace to MoneyPot/bustabit (Eric Springer, Jul 2014; rebranded Bustabit Apr 2015), which established provably-fair-via-hash-chain and a 1% house edge, and every descendant (Aviator, JetX, Stake Crash, BC.Game Crash) kept the house-banked model. Nobody has shipped player-set crash points because it is a lowest-unique-bid auction, and the LUBA literature (arXiv:1007.4264, arXiv:1702.08794) is explicit that observed play diverges wildly from equilibrium and that THE SELLER makes the money — i.e. the rake-taker wins and the players lose, the opposite of a skill narrative. Solana crash games already exist and are marketed as gambling (solanacrash.io, crashout.fun, rugs.fun). rugs.fun is the cautionary tale: a Feb 2026 expose alleged the entire price sequence is computed before bets are placed and merely animated back — exactly the trust failure Fuse claims to solve — and it did not stop rugs.fun operating, evidence that provable fairness is not what this audience buys on. Skillz is the flagship compliant skill-wagering platform and its stock is down ~99% from the 2021 SPAC peak. Sources: crashgamesplay.com/guides/crash-game-history/ ; arxiv.org/pdf/1007.4264 ; docs.skillz.com/docs/28.0.5/legal-skillz/ ; medium.com/@rugsfraud/rugs-fun-the-fraud-the-lies-3eb859f39342
critique.suggestedFix: Make detonation second-price (Vickrey): the round ends at the SECOND-lowest un-cashed fuse, and the owner of the LOWEST fuse is the detonator, earning 2x that second-lowest value. This is the textbook cure for epsilon-undercutting — your reward is set by someone else's number, so shaving 0.01 buys you nothing, the fuse distribution stops collapsing to the floor, and the multiplier actually climbs. Stack one guard on top: detonator points = 2 * (M* - 1.00) * (number of players who cashed out), so ending the round at 1.01 with zero cashouts pays literally zero and the floor rush is priced out. Then, separately and non-negotiably: ship it free-to-play with fake points, no wallet, no chain, as a plain web game. If the mechanic is fun there you will know in a weekend for $0 instead of after five weeks of ER plumbing and a $50k legal opinion — and if it IS fun with fake points, you have learned the blockchain was never the product.

name: Commons
pitch: A hundred strangers get ten action points a day for seven days, and the only way to survive is to make promises you can prove you kept — or prove you broke.
coreLoop: One decision per day, thirty seconds to make it, twenty-three and a half hours to scheme about it. Each day you split 10 action points across FARM / RAID / GUARD / SHARE and commit the hash on-chain. FARM yields 2.0 food per point but with a congestion multiplier of 1/(1 + totalFarmPoints/400), so a table where everyone farms starves together. RAID takes 1.5 food per point from a wallet you name explicitly, reduced 1:1 by that target's GUARD points; multiple raiders on one target split what's actually there. GUARD is pure insurance and every unspent guard point is wasted. SHARE goes to a communal granary that pays back 3.0 food per share point — but ONLY if the table's total SHARE that day hits 250 points; below the threshold the granary pays zero and the shared food is simply gone. Upkeep is 8 food per player per day; hit zero and you're eliminated, your seat burns, your PDA closes and its rent deposit refunds. Reveal window is 22:00–00:00 UTC, resolution by crank at midnight. Miss the reveal and your points default to 10 FARM plus a permanent −2 trust mark on your public record. The whole game is that SHARE is the only positive-sum move and it only works if a quarter of the table does it on the same night, which requires coordination the game gives you no tools for — you have to go do it on Twitter.
whyOnChain: This is the strongest whyOnChain of the three and it's one primitive: verifiable pre-commitment. In seven-day Diplomacy the entire currency is trust, and in every Web2 version of Diplomacy ever built a promise is worth nothing because you can change your order after you make the promise. Here you post your commit hash at 14:00, screenshot it in the alliance's Telegram, and at 00:00 the reveal proves you had already locked GUARD on your ally before you told them you would. You can make a promise that is mechanically impossible to break. Nobody can build that without a public, timestamped, tamper-evident ledger — and critically, neither can I: I can't peek at commits, can't reorder reveals, can't quietly favor a whale, and every player can verify that after the fact. The second on-chain-only property is portable reputation with a forgery cost: your season badges are soulbound cNFTs on your wallet, readable by anyone via DAS API, so the guy who sold out his alliance in Season 3 cannot rejoin Season 4 as a fresh Discord account. In a Web2 game, reputation resets with a new email; here resetting costs you a new wallet with no history, which is exactly the signal you want. Sybil resistance rides on the same rail via a small seat bond plus optional Solana Attestation Service checks.
solanaPrimitives: Per-player PDA per season (one 96-byte account each) — this shards writes so the game never touches a hot global account and never approaches the 12M CU per-writable-account per-block ceiling; priority fees stay near zero because Solana fee markets are local to writable accounts
Commit-reveal on L1 with the seat bond taken at seat purchase, not at reveal — the Switchboard rule about collateral timing applies to any commit scheme, otherwise losers simply never reveal
MagicBlock Cranks — the 00:00 UTC resolution fires as an automated on-chain instruction; a permissionless fallback lets any player call resolve for a small SOL bounty if the crank misses

Chunked resolution across 4+1 transactions — 100 player PDAs blows straight through the 64-accounts-per-tx lock limit, so resolve accumulates into an aggregate PDA in chunks and then finalizes; this is a hard constraint, not an optimization

Bubblegum V2 soulbound compressed NFTs (mpl-bubblegum 5.1.0) — survivor badges stamped with season, final food, betrayal count; soulbound + freeze are native in V2, and a 1M-leaf tree costs ~$500 versus $15–30k in rent for individual accounts
DAS API (Helius/Triton) for cross-season reputation lookup — a hard vendor dependency, since there is no getAccountInfo path to a cNFT
@solana/kit 7.1.1 with the new React hooks + Wallet Standard discovery; Codama 0.13.1 for the typed client off the IDL
Kora fee relayer — a player's total SOL requirement is the seat fee; gas is sponsored, so nobody bounces on 'insufficient SOL for fees'
Anchor 1.1.2, LiteSVM 0.15.2 for the seven-day payoff simulation (a full 100-player season replays in seconds in-process, which is how I balance it)
moneyFlow: IN: 0.1 SOL (~$8) per seat, one time, non-refundable — a ticket to a seven-day event, not a stake. That is the entire inflow. OUT: nothing. There is NO prize pool, NO payout, NO token. The reward for winning is a soulbound badge that cannot be sold, and the reason that's acceptable is that the reward people actually want is having beaten 99 people in public. Studio revenue = 10 SOL/season/table (~$800); run six parallel tables and a season every ten days and that's ~$14k/month — genuinely small, and I'd rather say that plainly than model a fantasy. SINKS: seat fee is consumed; food is a closed internal unit that never leaves the game, never trades, has no market and no price; upkeep burns 800 food/day off the table and the granary destroys shared food outright whenever the 250-point threshold misses. The economy is deflationary by construction and cannot ponzi because there is no faucet paying out anything of value. Legally this is Tier 0: consideration exists but there is no prize of value, so the three-element gambling test fails at the prize prong, and because I issue no token and sell no appreciating asset there's no securities surface either. Rent: every player PDA is closed at season end and its ~0.002 SOL deposit refunded, which also cleans up state.
firstSession: 0:00 — you see a CT thread: someone posting a screenshot of a commit hash with the caption 'this is me locking GUARD on @x tonight, verify at midnight.' You click through to commons.game. 0:30 — the landing page is the live table: 100 rows, each showing a wallet, food count, days survived, and a red RAIDED or blue SHARED tag from last night's resolution, plus one number in huge type — 'LAST NIGHT'S SHARE: 218 / 250. GRANARY LOOTED.' You can read the entire game state without an account. 1:00 — 'TAKE A SEAT — NEXT SEASON STARTS IN 3 DAYS' → Wallet Standard → Phantom → one tx, 0.1 SOL, which creates your player PDA. No email, no username; your wallet is your name. 1:30 — the rules are one screen: four moves, five numbers, one threshold. You read it in ninety seconds because there are only five numbers. 2:00 — you're dropped into the season Telegram link and the CT hashtag, and there is nothing else to do for three days except talk to 99 strangers. 2:00 onward — the real onboarding is that someone DMs you within an hour asking you to guard them, and you have to decide whether a stranger's word means anything. Day 1, 23:00 UTC: you spend thirty seconds allocating 10 points and hit commit. That's the whole session. It costs you thirty seconds a day and occupies your entire brain for a week.
viralMechanic: The game deliberately ships with no chat, no forum, no in-game messaging. All 100 players must negotiate on public Crypto Twitter and in Telegram DMs, which means the game's diplomacy layer IS a content firehose on the platform I need to grow on, and it costs me nothing to build. Then the commit hash turns every alliance into a public, verifiable, timestamped drama: you post your hash as proof of a promise, and at 00:00 UTC the chain publishes whether you kept it. A betrayal is not a claim someone makes — it's a cryptographic receipt with a block height, and receipts get quote-tweeted. Each midnight resolution generates a single shareable image (the table, the survivors, the eliminated, and the night's biggest betrayal) posted automatically, so there are seven scheduled viral moments per season whether I do anything or not. Player A drags in player B structurally because alliances need bodies: a bloc of 25 is the only way to hit the SHARE threshold, and recruiting for your bloc is the dominant strategy on days 1–3. Eliminated players stay engaged because they can still talk, and a bitter eliminated player is the loudest poster on the table.
mvpScope: 4 weeks solo — this is the cheapest of the three to build because there is no real-time layer at all. IN: one Anchor program (buy_seat, commit, reveal, resolve_chunk, finalize, close_seat); the payoff function written and balanced entirely in LiteSVM by simulating thousands of 100-player seasons against scripted archetypes (all-farm, all-raid, cartel-of-25, chaos) before a line of client code exists — this is where three of the four weeks of design value lives; a client that is one HTML table, one allocation form, and a countdown; the crank plus the permissionless-resolve fallback; a Helius webhook writing resolutions to SQLite for the public table. CUT for v1: the soulbound cNFT badges (add in week 5 — season 1 survivors get theirs retroactively, which is itself a nice post), cross-season reputation UI, multiple concurrent tables, any chat, mobile-native, Solana Attestation Service integration, elimination-round spectator modes. Hard scope rule: five numbers in the payoff matrix, and if a balance change needs a sixth number I cut a mechanic instead.
biggestRisk: Table collapse from attrition. The game needs 100 humans to show up for thirty seconds a day for seven consecutive days, and a Web3 audience's honest retention curve says day 3 is where half of them stop caring — and unlike a normal game, one player going dark degrades the experience for everyone allied to them. The 0.1 SOL seat fee is a bond meant to buy a couple of days of stubbornness and it is probably not enough. Mitigations are all design-side: the default-to-FARM-on-no-reveal rule keeps the table mechanically alive with absentees; elimination is framed as content rather than failure so the eliminated stay in the Telegram and keep talking; seven days is deliberately shorter than any comparable Diplomacy format. But I should be honest that the failure mode isn't 'nobody comes' — it's 'forty people come, it's electric for three days, and then it fizzles into eleven people farming quietly,' which is a bad screenshot and kills season 2. Second risk: this game lives or dies on whether the initial 100 include five loud, funny, scheming posters. If season 1 is a hundred quiet wallets, there's no content, and no amount of good payoff-matrix design fixes that — so season 1 seats should be hand-invited from CT, not sold open.

critique.name: Commons
technicalBlockers: The payoff matrix has a strict, Pareto-optimal, publicly-observable cooperative equilibrium that deletes the game by night 2. SHARE pays 3.0 food/point with NO congestion term. FARM pays 2.0/(1 + F/400), at most 2.0 and collapsing fast. RAID pays at most 1.5/point and is contested and guardable. GUARD pays 0. So whenever the 250-point threshold clears, SHARE strictly dominates every other verb for every player — and the threshold clears trivially: 250 of 1000 table AP is an average of 2.5 of 10 points each.

Risk-dominance says cooperation locks in immediately. Share EV = 3p; farm EV against a mostly-sharing table (F near 0) = 2.0. Share whenever p > 0.667. After night 1's public resolution shows SHARE at or near 1000, p is ~1 forever. No betrayal, no elimination, no drama, no midnight image, no CT firehose. The product thesis rests on an equilibrium the numbers forbid.

Run the cooperative table: all 1000 AP to SHARE yields 3,000 food against 800 upkeep = +2,200 food/day. Over 7 days that is +15,400 food across 100 players = 154 food each against 8/day upkeep — 19 days of buffer accumulated inside a 7-day season. Nobody is ever eliminated; the elimination mechanic never fires.

The opposite failure is latent and worse. FARM output is 800F/(400+F), monotone increasing, and with F capped at 1000 the table maximum is 571.4 food/day against 800 food/day of upkeep. Farming can NEVER cover upkeep at any allocation. So if SHARE ever misses the threshold the table loses at least 229 food/day with no counterplay and spirals to mass elimination. The game has exactly two states — trivial abundance or unavoidable death — and nothing in between.

THE COMMITMENT IS NOT BINDING, which kills the sole whyOnChain. Reveal is optional; the penalty is 10 FARM plus a cosmetic -2 trust mark, and the seat bond is taken ONCE at seat purchase, not per round. So a player watches 90 reveals land during the 22:00-00:00 window and, if their committed move is now bad, simply declines to reveal. Concrete: you committed 10 RAID on Alice; reveals show 8 co-raiders splitting her stack; your take drops from 15 food to ~1.9; you decline and take 10 FARM (~5.7 food at F=1000) instead, netting ~+4 food for a cosmetic mark. This violates the exact Switchboard rule the pitch cites — collateral at commit time, not reveal time — because there is no per-round collateral to slash. 'A promise mechanically impossible to break' is false: you break it by staying silent.

Public rolling reveals leak the board. Because reveals land in the clear across a 2-hour window, the last revealer has full information on 99 opponents. They cannot change their commit, but they hold a free option on whether to execute it, and that option has positive value every single night.

The chunked-resolution plan is under-specified in a way that will cost a week. Raid edges are arbitrary (any player names any wallet), so you CANNOT partition 100 PDAs into chunks with raider and target co-located. You must accumulate all reveals into an aggregate PDA first (100 * ~68 bytes = ~6.8 KB — fine, allocate once, under the 10,240-byte realloc cap), then compute globally, then write back. Multi-raider splitting is O(n^2) = 10,000 pairs at ~30 CU = ~300k CU, which blows the 200k default per-instruction limit and needs an explicit ComputeBudget request in a dedicated 1.4M-CU tx. Realistic shape is 2 accumulate + 1 compute + 2 write-back = 5 txs with explicit phase guards, not '4+1'. The permissionless resolve fallback must also be a hard state machine or a griefer runs 3 of 5 steps and leaves the table half-resolved.
economicHoles: Reputation costs $8 to reset, which is the entire seat price. The claim that 'the guy who sold out his alliance in Season 3 cannot rejoin Season 4 as a fresh Discord account' is simply wrong — he rejoins as a fresh WALLET for 0.1 SOL, the same price everyone else pays. The forgery cost of identity is set exactly equal to the price of admission, and it has to be, because you need to fill 100 seats.

A single $200 actor is a dictator over the only positive-sum mechanic. The SHARE threshold is 250 points = exactly 25 players * 10 AP. Buying 25 of 100 seats costs 2.5 SOL (~$200) and confers unilateral control over whether the granary pays each night, in either direction. In a 100-seat game at $8/seat, blocking minorities are pocket change.

Working reputation is anti-content for a betrayal game. Every long-running Diplomacy community rediscovers this: permanent, cryptographically-attested betrayal records make players stop betraying, which removes the thing people came for. You are building a mechanic that suppresses your own content engine and then relying on that content for all your distribution.

Revenue is $800/table-season with no prize. Six tables per 10-day cycle = ~$14.4k/mo, requiring ~1,800 people/month to pay $8 for a soulbound badge and a text table, against a backdrop of 93% of web3 games dead and studio funding down 93%. By their own plan season 1 seats are hand-invited rather than sold, so season 1 revenue is $0 and the retention thesis stays untested until season 2 — which they correctly identify as the whole business.

Bots are trivial here but mostly harmless, which is the tell: if a script plays optimally (allocate 10 SHARE, reveal on schedule) the game's decision content is near zero. A game whose optimal policy is a one-line cron job does not hold 100 humans for seven days.
legalFlags: Genuinely clean on gambling, and the reasoning is right: consideration exists, chance is arguable, but there is no prize of value, so the three-element test fails at the prize prong. No token, no appreciating asset, no securities surface. This is the only one of the three with a defensible Tier 0 posture — protect it by never adding a prize pool, because a prize flips the entire analysis in one commit.

Permanent, immutable, public 'betrayal count' and -2 trust marks attested to wallets create a GDPR right-to-erasure conflict for EU players, and the record is by design un-erasable. Low probability, but you are choosing a data model with no deletion path for adverse personal characterizations.

Minor: non-refundable $8 entry to a timed elimination event with no prize is a sale of a service, not a contest — fine — but the moment seats become resellable or badges become transferable you acquire a secondary-market story you have not analyzed. Keeping badges soulbound (Bubblegum V2 soulbound is the right call) is load-bearing legal design, not a nicety.
critique.priorArt: Dark Forest (Brian Gu / gubsheep, 2020) is the direct reference: the most technically acclaimed fully-on-chain hidden-information strategy game ever built, ZK fog of war, MIT Technology Review coverage, a genuine proof that cryptographic commitment can carry a game. The original is no longer playable; the IP moved to the 0xPARC Foundation and the successor is Dark Frontier by Argus Labs. It never sustained a persistent player base despite being the best possible execution of exactly this thesis — the single most relevant data point for Commons, and it is not encouraging. On the Diplomacy side, webDiplomacy and Backstabbr have run free-entry multiplayer Diplomacy for ~20 years and their permanent, well-documented failure mode is exactly the stated biggest risk: mid-game abandonment degrading the board for everyone allied to the absentee. Twenty years of prior art says an $8 bond does not fix that. No prior art found for a paid-seat, reputation-persistent, on-chain Diplomacy season. Sources: naavik.co/deep-dives/dark-forest-beacon-of-light/ ; technologyreview.com/2022/11/10/1062981/dark-forest-blockchain-video-game-creates-metaverse/ ; coindesk.com/markets/2026/04/23/more-than-90-of-web3-games-failed-after-usd15-billion-boom-as-gamers-never-showed-up-caladan
critique.suggestedFix: Make SHARE an actual public good instead of a coordinated self-payment. Right now SHARE pays 3.0 food back TO THE CONTRIBUTOR, which makes it individually dominant and turns a cooperation game into a solved optimization. Change it so share points produce food distributed EQUALLY across all 100 players regardless of who contributed — 10 points contributed yields you ~0.3 food and yields the table 30. Now free-riding is individually correct, cooperation is socially correct, and the game you advertised (coordination the mechanics refuse to help you with) actually exists. Pair it with two forced corrections: rebalance FARM so a defecting minority can at least tread water (max farm output must exceed the 800 upkeep, not sit at 571), otherwise the non-cooperative branch is an unwinnable death spiral; and take a per-round food bond at COMMIT that is forfeited on non-reveal so the commitment is genuinely binding — or ship reveals through the Private ER/TEE you cut, so nobody sees any reveal until all 100 are in. Without one of those two, the pre-commitment thesis is decoration.

name: Drawdown
pitch: One aquifer, ten thousand pumps, and a number on the front page counting down to the moment everyone's greed drains it dry.
coreLoop: Thirty seconds, and it's the Cookie Clicker loop with a knife in it. You have one pump. It draws water while you're gone. You come back, claim what accumulated, and choose: spend it on the next pump level (cost 100 × 1.6^level, each level ×1.5 draw rate) or BOTTLE it, which banks it permanently as score and removes it from the game forever. Classic greed-versus-compounding — except the rate isn't yours. The aquifer starts each season at 1,000,000,000 units and recharges at 20,000/second, fixed and public. Your effective draw is your nominal rate × T², where T is the fraction of the aquifer remaining. So when the table is at 80% you're drawing at 64% efficiency; at 20% you're at 4% and your beautiful level-24 pump is producing almost nothing. Aggregate draw is visible to everyone as a live gauge on the front page with a countdown: 'DRY IN 4H 11M.' Every player individually wants to pump harder; collectively that quadratic collapse is a cliff everyone can see coming and nobody can stop alone. Which is why you can form a BASIN — a named group of up to 50 wallets whose combined bottled total ranks on a team leaderboard, and which can vote to impose a self-throttle that the program actually ENFORCES on its members' draw rates. A basin that throttles keeps the aquifer alive longer and out-scores everyone at the end; a member who leaves the basin to sprint is publicly visible on-chain the second they do it. Season ends when the aquifer hits zero, roughly 6–9 days depending on how greedy the crowd is, and the final bottled leaderboard is the season's permanent record.
whyOnChain: Moderate and I'll grade it honestly rather than oversell it. The loop itself would work fine in Web2 — this is not a game that is impossible without a chain. What the chain supplies is the one thing the game is entirely about: credible scarcity. A tragedy-of-the-commons game only generates tension if every player genuinely believes the operator will not quietly refill the well, will not hand a sponsor a bigger pump, and will not extend the season when the numbers look bad — and in Web2 you simply have to take my word for it, which is worth nothing, and the moment anyone suspects a fudge the entire emotional premise evaporates. Here the aquifer is a PDA with a hardcoded initial reserve, the recharge is a constant in a program with a timelocked (later revoked) upgrade authority, and any player can read the reserve and the total draw at any block. That is the research's one honest asset claim — not 'you own your items' but 'the issuer cannot secretly print more' — applied to the resource instead of to a token. The second genuine add is the basin throttle: an enforced cartel. A Web2 guild can pinky-swear to slow down; an on-chain basin has its members' rate cap enforced by the program, which turns a coordination problem with no teeth into a real institution players can build, defect from, and be caught defecting from. That's a mechanic Web2 cannot express. If you stripped both of those out you'd have a decent idle game and I'd call it a Web2 game with a wallet.
solanaPrimitives: MagicBlock Ephemeral Rollup — the entire aquifer, including the single hot global reserve account, is delegated to the ER, which sidesteps the 12M CU per-writable-account per-block ceiling that would otherwise cap the whole game at a few hundred claims per block on L1; state commits to L1 hourly (0.0001 SOL/commit) and on season end via undelegation

L1 fallback architecture if the ER is unavailable: 64 sharded aquifer PDAs assigned by pubkey % 64, with a crank rebalancing shards every 30 slots — named here because the naive single-global-account design is the single most common way a Solana game dies, and it dies at exactly 12M CU
MagicBlock Cranks — hourly L1 commits, season rollover, and basin throttle enforcement windows run as automated on-chain instructions with no server of mine in the loop

MagicBlock VRF in-ER (free, <50ms) — seeds the NEXT season's recharge rate and upgrade cost curve within published bounds so the meta can't be solved once and copy-pasted; no value attaches to any roll, so this is randomness with no gambling surface

Kora fee relayer (Apr 2026) + Privy embedded wallets — this is the one of the three with a normie funnel, so the target is zero-SOL onboarding: click, play, and the pump PDA's ~0.002 SOL rent-exemption deposit is fronted and refunded to me when you close it at season end

Metaplex Core (mpl-core 1.10.0) for cosmetic pump skins at ~0.0029 SOL/asset — ~80% cheaper than Token Metadata, single-account model, and they trade on Magic Eden and show up in Backpack without me building a marketplace, which is the free-composability argument in its only honest form
Basin group PDAs with program-enforced draw caps — the cartel is a smart contract, not an honor system
Anchor 1.1.2 for the season/basin logic, Pinocchio 0.11.2 for the per-claim hot path, Mollusk 0.15.0 CU benchmarks in CI since claim cost is the per-player unit economics
moneyFlow: IN: nothing required to play. Optional: a $10 USDC season pass (one cosmetic skin, a personal stats page, a basin-creation right) and $5 USDC cosmetic pump skins as Metaplex Core assets, plus a 3% royalty on secondary skin trades enforced by the Core royalty plugin. OUT: nothing. Water is not a token, never leaves the game, has no market, and cannot be sold — bottled water is a score, full stop. There is no prize pool at MVP. SINKS: the aquifer itself is the sink and it is absolute — every unit drawn is gone, upgrade spending destroys water permanently, and bottling removes it from circulation. There is no faucet other than the fixed recharge, which is why the economy mathematically cannot inflate: E (value paid out) is identically zero, so E ≤ S + X − C holds trivially. This is Tier 0 legally: no prize of value, no chance attached to anything valuable, no token, no yield, no revenue share, no securities surface, and no money-transmission surface because value flows in and is consumed and never flows out to third parties. Unit economics: at 20,000 players with a 4% conversion on a $10 pass that's ~$8k/season at roughly three seasons a month. Costs: Helius ($499/mo tier, and I'd budget for DAS/LaserStream creeping up), MagicBlock ER session and commit fees (fractions of a cent per player-season), rent deposits which are recovered. The 'v2 with counsel' version puts a sponsor-funded USDC pot on the final bottled leaderboard — I am deliberately not shipping that in v1 because the moment there's a prize I inherit the entire contest-law analysis for a game that currently has none.
firstSession: 0:00 — a CT post with one image: a horizontal gauge at 6.8%, a red countdown reading 'DRY IN 0H 41M', and 'the aquifer is dying and 11,400 people are still pumping.' 0:10 — you land on drawdown.gg and the gauge is live and moving; you can see the number dropping. Below it: total pumps, top 10 basins, and the last 20 bottling events scrolling. Nothing gated. 0:30 — 'CLAIM YOUR PUMP.' No wallet screen: Privy embedded wallet, email or Google, done in one tap, and Kora sponsors the transaction so you are never told you need SOL. Your pump PDA exists ten seconds after you arrived. 0:45 — your pump reads LEVEL 1, DRAWING 0.04/s (because T is 0.068 and 1 × 0.068² is brutal) and you immediately understand the entire game from that one number: you showed up late and everyone before you already took it. 1:00 — you claim 12 units, which buys nothing, and the interface shows you the alternative: 'NEXT SEASON STARTS WHEN THIS ONE ENDS — 41 MINUTES.' 1:15 — you join a basin, because the basin leaderboard is the only thing that resets fairly and your basin is already recruiting for next season. 1:30 — you set a reminder for the season start. The first session's job is not to give you a good pump; it's to make you angry that you missed the beginning and desperate to be there at T=1.00. That is deliberate: a game with a visible countdown to zero converts latecomers into next-season pre-registrations, which is how a seasonal game builds a bigger cohort each time.
viralMechanic: The gauge is the mechanic. There is one public URL with one number falling in real time and a countdown to zero, viewable with no wallet, no login, and no install — it is a screenshot that explains itself, and it gets more dramatic the closer it gets to the end, which means the game's virality peaks exactly when a new cohort needs to register for the next season. Then the structural part: a naive idle game has anti-viral referrals, because every player you recruit lowers your own rate. Basins invert that. Your basin's score is the sum of its members' bottled water and it's capped at 50 wallets, so recruiting good players into YOUR basin is straightforwardly correct while recruiting into the world at large is a defection — every player is personally incentivized to run a private recruiting campaign for a named team with a public leaderboard position. Basins name themselves, trash-talk each other, and post their throttle votes as proof of discipline. The second content engine is betrayal-with-a-receipt: when a basin member breaks the throttle, the program logs it and the site publishes it, so 'BASIN CARTEL: member 0x… defected at 14:02, throttle broken, aquifer −4.1%' is an automatic post. No referral codes, no points, no airdrop expectation.
mvpScope: 5 weeks solo. IN: one Anchor program for seasons/pumps/basins with the claim path in Pinocchio; ER delegation of the aquifer plus hourly L1 commits; lazy accrual so a claim is one cheap tx that reads the global reserve and writes only your own PDA; the public gauge page (server-sent events off a Yellowstone gRPC subscription, no polling); the basin group PDA with a program-enforced rate cap and a simple majority vote; season rollover crank with in-ER VRF seeding next season's constants; Privy + Kora zero-friction onboarding; three cosmetic skins minted as Core assets. The economic tuning happens in LiteSVM before any client exists — simulate 10k agent-pumps under greedy/throttled/mixed populations to find a recharge rate and T² curve that yields a 6–9 day season under realistic greed. CUT: any prize pool (v2, with counsel), mobile app, chat, basin treasuries, pump trading, more than three skins, achievements, an account system, cross-season progression of any kind beyond your basin name and your leaderboard history. Hard rule: the game has exactly four verbs — claim, upgrade, bottle, join basin — and if a feature needs a fifth verb it doesn't ship.
biggestRisk: That it is a very good ten-hour game and a bad thirty-day game. Idle games die when the numbers stop surprising you, and the T² collapse means the second half of every season is mechanically worse than the first half — rates fall, upgrades stop paying back, and the correct play in the last two days is to bottle and stop logging in. Seasons are the answer, but seasonal resets are also how you churn people out permanently: if season 2 starts and the cohort is smaller than season 1's, the aquifer drains slower, the countdown is less dramatic, the screenshot is less good, and the whole thing deflates in public. The mitigation is that basins are the only persistent identity across seasons and the basin leaderboard is what people are actually competing on, but I won't know if that carries the meta until season 2, and season 2 is the whole business. Second, honest risk: the whyOnChain here is the weakest of the three. If a competent Web2 dev shipped this same loop with a nice gauge and no wallet, it would probably acquire faster and retain the same, and my only durable defense is that the scarcity is verifiable and the cartel is enforceable — which matters to the kind of player who reads a program's upgrade authority and to almost nobody else. I'd ship it anyway because the loop is fun and the gauge is a genuinely great CT artifact, but I would not tell anyone the blockchain is why it's fun.

critique.name: Drawdown
technicalBlockers: THE AQUIFER CAN NEVER REACH ZERO. Arithmetic, not opinion. dT/dt = (R - N*T^2)/S0. With recharge R=0 the solution is T(t) = 1/(1 + N*t/S0) — a 1/t decay reaching zero only as t goes to infinity. Any efficiency exponent p > 0 gives the same result: as T falls, aggregate draw falls faster than the remaining stock, so the drain decelerates without bound. 'DRY IN 4H 11M' is a linear extrapolation of an asymptotic curve; it will visibly slide right every hour, forever. Your one CT artifact is a clock that never fires, and players will screenshot THAT.

With the stated recharge there is no scarcity at all. R = 20,000/s over 24 hours = 1.728e9 units, which EXCEEDS the entire 1e9 initial reserve. The faucet replaces the whole aquifer every 13.9 hours; over a 7-day season it emits 1.21e10 = 12.1x the starting reserve. The aquifer is a flow, not a stock. The single claimed whyOnChain — 'the issuer cannot secretly print more' — is moot when the issuer is openly printing 12x the reserve per season by design.

The system converges to a fixed point, not an end: T* = sqrt(20000/N). From their own numbers (level 1 draws 0.04/s at T=0.068, so nominal_1 = 0.04/0.004624 = 8.65 units/s), driving T* to 5% needs aggregate nominal N = 8.0e6/s = ~925,000 level-1-equivalents — level ~12 each at 10,000 players (1.5^11.2), level ~16 each at 2,000 players. Season length is therefore not a design parameter, it is a knife-edge function of turnout: the one variable you do not control and cannot predict for season 2.

Lazy accrual is impossible as described, and the fix creates day-one MEV. Accrued water = nominal * integral of T(t)^2 dt, and T(t) depends on every other player's claims. You must maintain a global cumulative index (lending-protocol style) refreshed on every claim — so every claim WRITES the global aquifer account and the 'writes only your own PDA' plan does not hold. Worse, between refreshes the index uses a stale, higher T^2 and systematically over-credits. If T drifts 1.0 -> 0.9 inside one segment that is a 19% error in T^2. A bot claiming every ER slot keeps its own index fresh and captures accuracy idle players structurally lose — a free, permanent extraction against exactly the population the game is built for.

You are solving the wrong scaling problem and paying weeks for it. 20,000 players * ~6 claims/day = 120,000 claims/day = 1.39 claims/s. At ~8,000 CU per claim that is ~11,100 CU/s = ~3,900 CU per 350ms block against the 12M CU per-writable-account cap — 0.03% of the limit, three orders of magnitude away. The ER delegation and the 64-shard fallback are unnecessary, and the ER import brings the UNVERIFIED trust model, program-clone version skew, and broken L1 composability during delegation for zero throughput benefit. This is plain L1 with a Yellowstone subscription, and going ER probably costs 2 of your 5 weeks.

Idle games are solvable, and this one is solvable on day one. Four verbs, published constants, deterministic accrual — the optimal claim/upgrade/bottle policy is a small dynamic program. Someone posts the solver in the first 48 hours, everyone runs it, and the game becomes a spreadsheet with a gauge on top.
economicHoles: THE BASIN CARTEL HAS NO REASON TO EXIST, and it is your strongest claimed whyOnChain. Draw scales with T^2 globally, so a basin that throttles raises efficiency for EVERY player on the table. A 50-wallet basin in a 20,000-player game captures 50/20,000 = 0.25% of the externality its restraint creates while paying 100% of the cost. Program-enforced or not, unilateral throttling is a pure gift to non-members and is strictly dominated. You built a mechanism to enforce a cartel nobody is incentivized to form.

Kora + Privy + dev-fronted rent with no identity gate is an unbounded, free drain. Each pump PDA costs you ~0.002 SOL of rent plus sponsored fees, and a sybil never closes the account so the rent is never refunded. A for-loop creating 100,000 pumps costs the attacker approximately nothing and locks ~200 SOL = ~$16,000 of your SOL permanently — 2x your projected $8,000 seasonal revenue, burned in an afternoon, by one person. Sponsored gas with no rate limiter or attestation gate is a liability with no ceiling.

The basin leaderboard is the least sybil-resistant object in the game and it is also your entire retention thesis. Basin score = sum of members' bottled water, cap 50 wallets, wallet creation free and gasless. One operator fills a 50-wallet basin and tops the team leaderboard, which you designated as the only persistent cross-season identity. The individual leaderboard is actually fine (concentration beats splitting: 1.5^19 = 2,213 vs 50 level-1 pumps), which makes the contrast worse — you sybil-hardened the part that doesn't matter.

Latecomer design is a one-season trick. The 'you showed up at T=0.068 and everyone before you took it' anger converts to a next-season pre-registration exactly once. If season 2's cohort is smaller — which their own risk section concedes is likely — the aquifer drains slower, the gauge is less dramatic, the screenshot is worse, and the acquisition loop deflates in public. Season 2 is the entire business and the design has no answer for a shrinking cohort beyond hoping basins carry it.

Revenue is $8k/season on a 4% conversion of 20,000 players — a conversion rate and audience size that would put this in the top tier of Solana games. Against Helius at $499/mo plus LaserStream add-ons of $500-$6,000/mo, the margin is thin enough that one sybil wave is the difference between profit and loss.
legalFlags: Substantially correct that this is Tier 0: no prize of value, water never leaves the game, no token, no yield. The cleanest of the three, and the discipline of not shipping the sponsor-funded USDC pot in v1 is the single best judgment call across all three concepts. Keep it.

The 'no securities surface' claim is overstated. $5 cosmetics minted as Metaplex Core assets, with a dev-enforced 3% royalty, trading on Magic Eden, whose value depends on the developer continuing to run seasons, is materially closer to Friel v. Dapper Labs (S.D.N.Y. 2023 — NBA Top Shot Moments survived a motion to dismiss on Howey, largely because Dapper controlled the marketplace and the asset's value turned on Dapper's continued efforts) than to a Steam hat. Not fatal and unlikely to be enforced against a solo dev at this scale, but do not write 'no securities surface' in your own docs.

Distribution: mobile web and the Solana dApp Store (0% fee) are clean. If you ever ship to Google Play, in-app sales of NFT cosmetics for real money hit Play Billing policy, a repeated removal cause for web3 titles. The dApp Store's 1,561 apps is an uncontested channel and also a rounding error in reach — budget accordingly.
critique.priorArt: FOMO3D (Ethereum, 2018) is the direct ancestor and the outcome is the warning. Same structure: a single public, deterministic countdown to a pot, visible to everyone, drained by collective greed, marketed explicitly as 'a psychological social experiment in greed.' Round 1 ended on 22 Aug 2018 when address 0xa16...f85 block-stuffed Ethereum for ~180 seconds to be the last key buyer and took 10,469 ETH (~$3M) for an estimated $11,000-$13,800 in gas. The precedent is exact: a public deterministic countdown plus a leaderboard is an optimization problem, and the bot wins it. Wolf Game and the 2021-22 idle/GameFi cohort repeated the lesson at smaller scale. Broader context: Caladan classifies 93% of web3 game projects as dead against $12-15B deployed, with 300+ titles shut down in 2025-2026 alone, and every post-mortem's diagnosis is that projects optimized financial mechanics over a reason to return tomorrow — precisely the failure mode Drawdown's own risk section names. No prior art found for a shared-quadratic-efficiency depleting commons with program-enforced guild throttles; that mechanic is genuinely novel, which is exactly why nobody has yet discovered it does not pay to use it. Sources: medium.com/coinmonks/how-the-winner-got-fomo3d-prize-a-detailed-explanation-b30a69b7813f ; solmaz.io/2018/10/18/anatomy-block-stuffing/ ; coindesk.com/markets/2026/04/23/more-than-90-of-web3-games-failed-after-usd15-billion-boom-as-gamers-never-showed-up-caladan
critique.suggestedFix: Fix termination first, because the countdown IS the product and it is currently mathematically unreachable. Two one-line changes: cut recharge from 20,000/s to ~330/s (roughly 0.2 * S0 / 604,800, so the faucet is a fifth of the reserve over a week instead of twelve times it), and define season end as a hard T <= 0.02 cutoff, since no positive efficiency exponent ever reaches zero. Then fix the basin, the only mechanic that justifies being on a chain at all: as written, throttling gifts 99.75% of its benefit to non-members and will never be used. Make final basin score scale with the aquifer's terminal T — e.g. basin_score = sum(bottled) * (1 + k*T_final) — so a basin that keeps the well alive is paid for the externality it created, restraint becomes individually rational for the group exercising it, and defection becomes a genuinely costly public betrayal instead of a free lunch. Before either: gate account creation behind the $10 season pass or a Solana Attestation Service check, because sponsored gas plus dev-fronted rent with no identity is a free, unbounded drain on the only money in the system.
